  • Frightened: When Frightened, all tasks increase in Difficulty by 1 and you cannot willingly move towards the source of your Fear.
  • Immobilized: When Immobilized, your Speed is 0 and you cannot take any Voluntary Movement or Stand.
  • Incapacitated: When incapacitated, you cannot take any Actions or Reactions, and you cannot move. All attacks made against you gain a bonus d20.
  • Invisible: When invisible, creatures cannot see you, although your approximate location (which Space you are in) is still obvious unless you hide as normal.
  • Off-Guard: When Off-Guard, all tasks to defend increase in Difficulty by 1.
  • Prone: While prone, the Difficulty of all ranged attacks against you increases by +1, melee attacks gain +1d20 against you, and you cannot attempt any movement-related Major Actions. While prone, when you move, you crawl instead of walking, and each tile of movement costs 3 spaces of speed instead of 1. This status is removed if you stand.
  • Rattled: When Rattled, all tasks increase in Difficulty by 1. This status can be cleared as soon as you regain any Willpower.
  • Slowed: When Slowed, your Speed is halved.
  • Weakened: While Weakened, all of your melee, ranged, and spell attacks deal -2[CD] damage.

Visibility and Hidden Characters

In battle, characters may attempt to become unseen in order to gain an advantage over their opponents. When attempting a Task against a target that you cannot see, you have +1 Difficulty. This is true even if you know the target’s approximate location; for example, you would still have +1 Difficulty against an Invisible unit even if they turned Invisible right in front of you and didn’t move.

Characters or targets that are hidden cannot be the target of Tasks (such as a melee attack or spell) until they are found, which can be accomplished by using the Search Major Action, or until they take a hostile action against another character. Characters may become hidden by using the Hide Major Action, but can only successfully Hide if they are in Cover or Invisible. A successful Search action to find a hidden character will only reveal the target to the unit that performed the Search action.

Resistance and Cover

Characters are not entirely defenseless, and may make use of a variety of factors to protect themselves. Protection granted by armor is called Resistance, and it reduces the amount of damage inflicted. Protection from the terrain is called Cover, and it makes certain types of attacks against a character more difficult.

Resistance is measured by a static number, granted to you by your armor. Some effects and abilities may also grant additional resistance under specific circumstances, called Temporary Resistance, which stacks on top of any resistance you already have. After the damage has been rolled for an attack, the total damage inflicted is reduced by an amount equal to the character’s Resistance. If this final total is 0 or less, the attack has no further effect. If the final total is 1 or higher, then some damage has gotten through.

Protection granted by terrain or battlefield obstructions comes in one of two forms: Half Cover, or Full Cover. A character benefits from Half Cover if they are standing next to an obstacle that covers at least half their body, like a low wall or large bush. Being in Half Cover increases the Difficulty of ranged attacks against your character by +1. A character benefits from Full Cover if they are completely concealed by an obstacle, such as standing behind a large wall or a thick tree trunk. Full Cover prevents characters from being targeted by attacks that require line of sight, though they may still be affected by some attacks with areas of effect.

A character can only gain the benefit from being in Cover if the obstacle is directly between them and their attacker. If a character is in half cover thanks to being next to a bush and a ranged attacker moves around the bush to draw direct line of sight to them, that attacker does not receive +1 Difficulty on that attack. It is possible for a character to benefit from Half Cover against certain enemies, while having no cover from others. Characters cannot grant other characters full cover, though they may grant half cover to units that are adjacent if they are standing directly between them and an attacker.

Environments and Distance

An environment represents the “battlefield”—in short, the location a conflict is taking place within. This may be a building, a city street, an area of wilderness, part of a ship, or other such areas. In Ascension, all battlefields are represented using a gridded map divided into a large number of spaces, usually between 20x20 and 40x40. Spaces on the battlefield do not represent a specific distance, instead are a tactical unit that can be scaled up or down as the context of the battle necessitates, allowing a battlefield to represent an intimate courtyard or a wide valley without requiring exponentially large maps.

Knowing a character’s location and where they’re positioned relative to everyone else is critical to making tactical decisions in combat. All units (both player characters and NPCs) on the battlefield are represented by a token of some kind. Humans and creatures of a similar size or smaller occupy one space on the map. Larger characters may take up more than one space depending on their size. As characters move around on the battlefield, their token is moved to display their location.

The Gamemaster may create features or obstacles on the battlefield that impact the navigability of the environment by making it easier or more difficult to move around, gain cover, interact with objects, etc., denoting them clearly on the battlefield ahead of time. They may also mark parts of the environment as varying types of Terrain (as described below), which can alter the way characters can move across that region of the battlefield and affect how they engage with it tactically.

Movement

Your character has a Speed equal to 3 + Half your Agility (rounded down). On your turn, you can move by taking the Move Minor Action or the Sprint Major Action. Other abilities may provide other sources of movement. If you are prone, you crawl instead of walking, with each tile of movement costing 3 spaces of speed instead of 1.

Any time an effect allows you to move, it counts as Voluntary Movement unless explicitly stated.

The rules for diagonal movement are different if your battlemap uses squares instead of hexes. The first time you move into a diagonal square on your turn costs 1 Square of movement. The next time on that turn costs 2 squares of Speed, and alternates between the two thereafter.

Teleportation

Some Characters can Teleport, usually through the means of a Magick Spell. Teleportation is a type of movement that allows a character to instantly move from one space to another free space. Since Teleportation is a type of movement, Characters that are unable to move (such as from being Immobilized) cannot Teleport. Teleportation out of a Character’s Reach does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

Flying

In Ascension, the only spaces that a character can occupy are the spaces denoted on the map. As such, even if they have a flying speed, flying characters cannot occupy spaces above the map, and are never out of Reach of melee attacks from attackers in adjacent spaces. Characters with flying speeds may move across the map unimpeded by terrain effects and may move between any elevated areas without needing to use the Climb action.

If a character is reduced to 0 HP, they must make a Difficulty 2 Coordination + Skirmish task to maintain flight—if they fail, they immediately fall.

The Difficulty to make an attack with a bow against flying Characters decreases by 1.

Terrain

Normal Terrain includes that of most interior floors, roads, flat or gently rolling fields, or any other terrain that is effortless to move across. Movement on normal terrain is standard.

Difficult Terrain includes that of craggy rocks, low knee-deep water, the floor of a demolished building, and other uneven terrain with obstacles. Every space of movement over, onto, and off of difficult terrain costs twice as much as standard.

  • Forest is any space where there is abundant foliage or similar obstacles in the path. Forest is a type of difficult terrain. While in forest, you gain Half Cover, and you may attempt to hide in any space, even if an enemy currently has line of sight on you.
  • Deep Water is any space with water between thigh and chest deep. Deep Water is a type of difficult terrain. All attack and defending tasks made in water have +2 Difficulty.
  • Perilous Water is any space with water shoulder deep or deeper. Perilous Water is a type of difficult terrain and counts as Deep Water. Movement over, onto, and out of Perilous Water costs three times as much as standard. When you start your turn in Perilous Water, take 4[CD] piercing damage.

Roads are paved areas of a map that make it easier to move from place to place. When you start your turn on a Road tile, you gain +1 Speed until the end of your turn. Flying units do not get this bonus.

Height

Terrain may also have different levels of elevation or buildings and walls of different heights. Characters can climb up or down buildings and objects at Height 1 using the Climb Minor Action. Anything taller than that is deemed impassable unless you or your mount can fly. A helpful way to think of the levels of elevation is in terms of stories, so a one story tall object would be Height 1, while a three story tall object would be Height 3.

Height

Example

1

A road barricade, a single-story house, a simple fence

2

A two story house, a town wall.

3

A three story tower, the walls around a keep.

Some maps with elevated terrain or objects will also have ways to traverse these obstacles without needing to fly.

  • Stairs and Light Slopes are spaces that act as normal terrain and allow you to move between areas that are one level of elevation difference.
  • Steep Slopes are spaces that allow you to move between areas that are one level of elevation difference, but count as difficult terrain if you are moving in the direction of the higher elevation.
  • Ladders are spaces that allow you to move between areas of any difference in height elevation without using the Climb Minor Action. Every level of height moved up on a ladder costs 2 movement. Every level of height moved down a ladder costs 1 movement.

Falling

When a character falls from a height, they take damage. For every level of height a character falls from, they take 2[CD] Piercing damage up to a maximum of Height 10. For example, a character who falls from a Height 5 tower would suffer 10[CD] Piercing damage. Any character who does not use the Climb action to get down from elevated terrain takes fall damage when moving.

Rest and Recovery

Unless they die, a character can recover from the damage they suffer. Characters are able to restore Willpower and HP during combat using Tasks and special abilities, potentially curing accumulated Wounds, but Injuries cannot be healed during combat and can only be treated outside of combat during rests.

Rests require at least an hour or so during which characters are not in immediate danger and can quickly recover and heal themselves. During a rest, characters can restore all of their missing Willpower and HP, and their Wounds go away. Additionally, during rests characters may take the Treat Injury task.

Example Round of Combat

The party of Lorenz, Adelinde, Erik, and Rylan are escorting a nobleman’s son to his wedding when they are attacked on the road by a group of bandits. Before the combat scenario begins, the party and the GM make note of the current totals in their Momentum and Threat pools in order to remember them for later, but these currencies will not be relevant during combat itself and are set aside. Each party member also checks their equipment and Lorenz checks his spell list to make sure that they have everything equipped that they want to use before combat begins. Lorenz decides that he wants to add a defensive spell to his prepared list, so swaps out Frigid Grasp for Arcane Parry on his prepared spell list.

Before anyone takes a turn, the GM marks the party’s deployment area on the map so the party can place their tokens there, and then places their own enemy unit tokens on the field. The party is facing an enemy band of two warriors, two bladesmen, two glaivemen, an archer, and an elementalist. Once the PCs have placed their tokens in the deployment area, the combat can begin.

Lorenz decides to take the first turn, wanting to capitalize on the way the enemy units are arranged on the field to cast an AOE attack spell. Using his Pyromancer 1 Talent, Lorenz uses a minor action to increase the area of effect of his next spell attack by 1. Then he uses his Major Action to cast the spell Fireball. Because of Pyromancer 1, Fireball now has Blast 3 instead of Blast 2, so Lorenz can target all enemy units within 3 spaces of the spell’s origin point. The two warriors and two bladesmen are 8 spaces away--within the spell’s range of 10--and standing close enough together that they can all be hit by this spell, so they all need to make Agility + Skirmish Tasks to defend. The bladesmen have targets of 14 and they gain an extra d20 when defending because they each have a shield. The first bladesman generates 3 Successes, the second bladesman generates 2. The warriors have targets of 11 and each only roll 2 dice. The first warrior gets a critical success on one of their dice and generates 3 successes, while the second warrior generates only 1 success. Once all of the enemy units have rolled, Lorenz gets to make his roll, a Reason + Skirmish Task. He has a Focus in Arcane Magick and a target number of 15, so generates a critical success with a 4, and one more success with a 15 for a total of 3 Successes. With 3 successes, all four of the enemy units fail, and Lorenz generates 0 bonus momentum because his Successes tied with the highest Successes of his opponent. Then he rolls 6CD to determine the damage for a total of 8 damage with 4 effects. Because Fireball has Piercing, the attack ignores the resistance of all four enemy units, dealing 8 damage to each of them directly. With his second minor action, Lorenz moves up to his Speed, and after that, Lorenz ends his turn.

After Lorenz, the GM takes their turn. They decide to have the archer go, who has the optional features Steady Aim and Skulker. First, the archer uses the Aim minor action to give their next attack +1d20 (Steady Aim) and a free reroll. Then they use their major action to make an attack against Adelinde. Adelinde makes her roll to defend using Awareness + Skirmish, which gives her a target number of 9. She gets a bonus die because of her Round Shield and rolls two 8s and a 19, generating 2 Successes. The archer then makes their own Awareness + Skirmish Task with a target of 15, generating only 2 Successes after they roll a 14, 7, and an 18.  Because they Aimed, however, the archer can reroll the 18, and gets a 9, generating 3 total successes. The archer successfully attacks Adelinde, but because they are an NPC in combat, the extra success does not generate any Threat. The archer rolls 7CD damage for a total of 8 damage with 1 effect. Adeline has 4 resistance, so after subtracting for resistance she only takes 4 damage directly, leaving her with 35/39 HP. After attacking, the archer uses their Skulker feature to Hide as a minor action. The archer makes a Difficulty 2 Agility + Intrigue Task, generating 2 Successes. Because they have hidden successfully, the archer cannot be targeted by attacks unless a unit uses the Search action to find them first.

Next, Erik takes his turn. Because he is using a greataxe, Erik’s attacks are defended by Agility, so he decides to take down the warriors and leave the bladesmen--who are better at Agility and thus more likely to successfully defend against him--for the rest of the party. First, Erik uses the Move minor action to move 8 spaces, putting him next to both of the warriors. Then he uses his major action to make an attack against one of the warriors. The warrior has to make an Agility + Skirmish Task, and generates 2 successes, then Erik makes his Brawn + Skirmish Task with a target of 15 and a Focus in Axes, generating 4 successes after rolling a 3 and a 4, generating 2 bonus Momentum. Then he rolls his 9CD damage, rerolling 3 of the blank dice he got for free thanks to his Axe Adept Talent, for a total of 14 damage and 2 effects. The warrior only had 1 HP left after Lorenz’ fireball, so they are defeated. With 2 bonus Momentum, Erik decides to spend them to take a Swift Task to make another attack against the second warrior. The warrior makes his task to defend, generating 0 successes. Erik rolls his two dice, getting 1 Success and generating 1 bonus Momentum. Then he rolls his 9CD, generating only 3 damage with 2 effects (and 6 blank CD), but spends the 1 bonus Momentum he generated to reroll the 6 blanks, getting a new total of 9 damage with 2 effects. Because the warrior has only 2 resistance and 1 HP left, that is enough damage to defeat them. After that, Erik uses his second minor action to Block to gain 2CD (he rolls 3) temporary HP until the start of his next turn.

Then it is back to the GM’s turn, who decides to make the elementalist go next. The elementalist has the optional feature Devastating Spells. First, the elementalist uses their minor action to Aim, giving them a reroll on a single die during their next attack, and uses their second minor action to give their attack +2CD damage. Then because he’s within 6 spaces of them, they use their major action to make an attack against Erik using the Electric Arc spell, which has range 6. Erik has to defend using Coordination + Skirmish, with a target of 11,  generating 2 successes. The elementalist makes a Reason + Skirmish task with a target of 14 to attack, generating only 2 successes and rolling a 20 on one of their dice, creating a Complication that gives the elementalist’s next Task +1 Difficulty. Because the elementalist and Erik tied, the elementalist’s attack is successful. Their spell has 7CD damage +2CD from Devastating Spells, so they roll 9CD total, generating 9 damage and 5 effects, and because the attack has Piercing, it also ignores resistance. Erik takes the 9 damage directly, which first depletes his temporary HP and then takes him to 39/45 HP. The elementalist then ends their turn.

Adelinde decides to go next. She uses her minor action to Move, and because she’s mounted on a horse her speed is 10, so she moves 10 spaces to get closer to the elementalist. Then, she uses her major action to Direct, ordering Rylan to attack one of the glaivemen. Rylan has a longbow, so the glaivemen defends using Awareness + Skirmish, with a target of 12, generating 2 successes. Rylan then makes their attack using Awareness + Skirmish with a target of 15, assisted by Adelinde’s Presence + Authority, with a target of 15. Rylan rolls a 20 and a 9, generating only 1 success and a Complication. Adelinde rolls a 3 on her assist die, generating 2 successes for 3 successes total, which generates 1 bonus Momentum plus an additional 1 bonus momentum because Adelinde has a Banner. Because of the Complication, Rylan’s next Task will have +1 Difficulty. Then Rylan rolls their 7CD damage, generating 7 damage and 3 effects, and they use the bonus momentum to add +2 damage for a total of 9. The glaiveman has 2 resistance, so they take 7 damage, defeating them. Adelinde ends her turn.

On the GM’s turn, they have the remaining glaiveman take their turn. The glaiveman takes the Move minor action to get within range of Adelinde, then uses their major action to make an attack against her. Adelinde defends with her Brawn + Skirmish with a target of 13, and she adds a bonus die because of her Round Shield, generating 3 successes. The glaiveman makes their Coordination + Skirmish attack with a target of 14, generating only 2 successes. Because they rolled below the opposed task’s Difficulty, the glaiveman fails and Adelinde has a melee weapon, she gets to deal counterstrike damage to them in return, generating 1 bonus Momentum because she rolled above the glaiveman’s number of Successes. She rolls 5CD, 3 damage and 1 effect with 3 blank dice. Adelinde spends her bonus momentum to reroll the blanks, getting a new total of 6 damage and 2 effects. Because the glaiveman has 2 resistance, they take 4 damage, bringing them to 3/7 HP. The glaiveman then ends their turn without using their second minor action.

Finally, it is Rylan’s turn. First, they use a minor action to Block, rolling 2CD to gain +2 temporary HP. Then, Rylan decides to focus on finishing off the glaiveman that Adelinde injured. Because they received a Complication earlier, they now have a +1 Difficulty to their next Task. Rylan uses their second minor action to Aim, which lets them reroll a die and choose between results because they have Bow Adept. They use their major action to make an attack against the glaiveman. The glaiveman rolls with Awareness + Skirmish, with a target number of 12, generating 1 success, but because of the Complication, Rylan’s Difficulty is 2. Rylan then makes their Awareness + Skirmish roll with a target number of 15, rolling a 2 and an 11. Rylan rerolls the 11 to see if he can roll a crit and gets an 18, but thanks to Bow Adept, he can still keep the 11, ultimately generating 3 Successes and gaining 1 bonus Momentum. Rylan rolls their 7CD, generating 5 damage and 2 effects, and they spend their bonus momentum to add +1 damage to the attack, dealing 6 damage, reduced to 4 by the glaiveman’s resistance but still enough to defeat the glaiveman..

After Rylan’s turn, the rest of the enemy units may go. Of the units still standing, only the two bladesmen haven't taken their turns yet. The bladesmen both have the optional feature Swift Strikes. The first bladesman uses a minor action to move next to Erik and their major action to attack him. Erik defends using Coordination + Skirmish with a target of 11, generating only 1 success. The bladesman then attacks with Agility + Skirmish with a target of 14, generating 2 successes. They roll 6CD damage for a total of 5 damage. Erik has 2 resistance, so he takes 3 damage. Because of the Swift Strikes feature, the bladesman immediately makes another attack against Erik. This time Erik doesn’t generate any successes, but the NPC generates 3, dealing another 6CD for a total of 6 damage. Because of Erik’s resistance, he only takes 4 damage, leaving him at 32/45 HP.

After the bladesman ends their turn, the other bladesman also moves and attacks Erik. This time, Erik generates more Successes than the bladesman and deals 9CD counterstrike damage for a total of 7 damage. Because the bladesman was already injured by Lorenz’ Fireball, this is enough damage to defeat them. After that, all of the enemy units have taken their turns or been defeated. At the end of the round, the GM deploys 2 more Glaivemen as reinforcements, and a new round begins.

Part Four: Items and Enhancements

Chapter Six: Talents

Talents are split into two categories: Narrative and Combat. Narrative Talents are special abilities that a character possesses which provide certain benefits to taking certain actions in narrative (non-combat) play, often enhancing the outcome of a character’s particular course of action if successful. They may not be used during combat scenes. Narrative Talents are categorized into groups called “Archetypes,” each related to a character’s role in society or a specific way in which they might navigate the world, e.g. “Scholar” or “Heir.” Characters can always choose Narrative Talents from any Archetype, so long as they meet any necessary requirements.

Combat Talents are special abilities and benefits that only apply when a character is involved in a combat scenario. Combat Talents are organized into different groupings called “Talent Trees,” which each have a number of tiers, with a different Talent at each tier. Characters must gain Combat Talents in the order of their tier, only unlocking higher tier Talents once they’ve gained the lower tier Talents. For example, in order to take Dual Wielding 3, a character must already have Dual Wielding 1 and Dual Wielding 2. Some Talent Trees may have different branches, in which the first Tier Talent unlocks two or more different Talents with their own succeeding Talent(s). Some Talent Trees may also have specific requirements that must be met before a character can take any of their Talents.

Characters cannot take a Tier 3 Combat Talent until ascending to Level 3.

Narrative Talents

Skill Archetypes

The following are the six archetypes based on Ascension’s six Skills.

Warrior

(Requires 3 Skirmish)

You’re a fighter, first and foremost, and know how to apply your skills on and off the battlefield.

Glare

When you would Assist an ally with a Diplomacy or Authority Task using Agility, Brawn, or Coordination, you may also use Skirmish in place of Diplomacy or Authority. When you use this ability, you may make the check with a bonus d20.

Go For a Walk

Once per session, when you separate from the group to do something alone—such as get a quick threatening word with an NPC, stealing an important item, or sabotaging a carriage—you can trigger this ability to automatically succeed on one Task. If you do so, you will leave a trace that clearly points back to you—you can easily succeed, but other Characters will find out that you did it.

Breaking Point

You know just what it takes to get on someone’s nerves to start a fight. When in a public setting, you can automatically succeed in riling a character up enough to get them to start a brawl and make it seem like it was their fault.

Never Show Fear

The heat of battle has taught you how to keep your emotions in check. You cannot be intimidated, and other characters have +1 Difficulty on Tasks to read your emotions.

Predator

You’ve marked someone as your prey, and you won’t let them escape. When you attempt a Task to follow or chase after someone using Skirmish and you succeed, your target cannot escape from you until you let them.

Captain

(Requires 3 Authority)

You have practice ordering people around.

Bolstering Word

Whenever you assist on a task using your Authority, you may roll two dice instead of one. In addition, you never have to spend Momentum in order to assist.

Recruiter

When performing a task to convince someone to join your cause or bow to your command, you gain an extra d20. You may always succeed at cost on any checks to learn what it would take to convince them.

That’s an Order

Once per scene, when you give instructions to a character who reports to you or is under your command, they must agree to obey or suffer a Complication.

Plan of Action

Whenever an ally succeeds on a Task that had its Difficulty lowered thanks to an Advantage you created, they generate two bonus momentum.

Let Me Try

Once per session, when someone in your party fails on a Task, before the GM narrates the consequences of their failure, you may attempt to salvage the situation. You reattempt the Task, using the Task’s original Attribute + your Authority. On a success, you negate the previously failed roll and the scene continues. If you also fail, you reap the consequences of failure and generate an additional Complication.

Diplomat

(Requires 3 Diplomacy)

You know how to talk your way through almost anything.

Keep Them Talking

When engaging someone in conversation, you have a knack for keeping them there. Anyone you talk to has an extra difficult time leaving the conversation if you don’t want them to, allowing you to stall them indefinitely, and must perform a contested Faith + Diplomacy task against you to leave. Additionally, if you fail a Chit-Chat task during Negotiation, the Difficulty of Persuade increases by +1 as normal instead of +2.

Translator

Your knowledge of multiple languages makes it easier to connect to strangers from foreign lands. When speaking with someone in a language that is not your primary native one, you may increase the Complication range of a Diplomacy Task by 2 in order to lower the Difficulty by 1, as if you were a native speaker of that language. If you roll a Complication, through some mistake of accent or grammar, you say something with an unintended meaning.

The Art of the Deal

You may always succeed at cost on a task to bargain or haggle with someone. When you succeed on the Persuade Task as part of a Negotiation, you may reroll up to 3 [CD] Favor without spending Momentum.

Conversational Gambler

When you perform a task with Presence, you may increase the complication range by 2 to roll an extra die. If you do so on a Persuade Task during a Negotiation Challenge, you may also roll +2[CD] Favor dice on a success.

Cultural Flexibility

When you encounter someone from an unfamiliar culture or travel to a new place, you automatically succeed on any Tasks made in order to learn about that culture’s customs or how to behave appropriately, and you gain 2 bonus momentum that must be spent on Obtain Information.

Scholar

(Requires 3 Study)

You are well read and contain a wealth of knowledge.

Polymath

You are widely educated in many fields, and can speak on them with confidence. Once per session, you may declare that you actually have some expertise in a relevant subject. You gain a single Focus in that subject for the remainder of the scene.

Historian

You are well-versed in the histories of your world and the rise and fall of its kingdoms. You do not need to spend Momentum when using Obtain Information to gather information about events that happened more than ten years ago.

Lecturer

You are learned in rhetoric and debate, and making arguments with carefully studied historical evidence to back you up. When you use Reason to make a Diplomacy or Authority Task, you may make the check with a bonus d20.

Facts and Logic

When you succeed on a Reason + Diplomacy Task to persuade another character or convince them of a certain course of action, you generate an extra point of Momentum that can be spent immediately or saved to the group pool.

Meticulous

Years of careful study have taught you how to be methodical and check for errors before attempting a Task. When you attempt a Task using Study for which you have a relevant focus, you may reroll any number of dice in your dice pool for the Task.

Healer

(Requires 3 Medicine)

You are trained to tend to the sick and injured.

Bedside Manner

When you interact with a patient or someone sick or injured, they naturally feel more at ease in your presence. When you speak with them, you are able to keep them distracted from whatever is afflicting them. Additionally, the Difficulty on any tasks to convince them to share a secret with you is reduced by 1.

Apothecary

You possess a deep knowledge of poisons, diseases, and the cures for them. When treating a drugged, poisoned, or ill patient, you always know the best antidote or medicine so long as you know what the affliction is. The GM will tell you how you can obtain/make the cure and how long you have to treat it. Additionally, whenever you want to craft a poison, you always know what ingredients are necessary and the best places for you to obtain them.

I’m a Doctor, Not a…

When you attempt a Task using Medicine that is not related to trying to heal or treat a patient and purchase extra dice with Threat or Momentum, you may reroll the purchased dice.

Autopsy

When you encounter a dead body, you automatically succeed on any Tasks to identify their cause of death. Knowing this information creates an Advantage that you may use to reduce the Difficulty of a Task to find the culprit of their death by 1.

In My Professional Opinion

When you give advice to an ally, they can choose to heed it or ignore it. If they heed your advice, the crit range on their next Task is equal to your Medicine. If they ignore it, the complication range on their next Task increases by 1.

Scoundrel

(Requires 3 Intrigue)

You’re a master of stealth and intrigue.

Lockpicker

Locked doors are no challenge for you. You can easily unlock and lock common locks with no task needed. For rare complex locks—the sorts that nobles use to lock their treasuries or guarded with magick—any task to unlock them is made with a bonus d20.

Eavesdropper

You are skilled at listening in to conversations that you aren't meant to hear. As long as you can hear someone speaking at a whisper, or can see their lips, you are able to clearly make out everything that they say. In any case, you have a bonus d20 on any Awareness tasks to listen in to conversations if it is a question whether it is audible to you.

Wallflower

You are adept at disappearing in plain sight, with others not noticing you ever left. If at least 2 Allies are with you during a scene, you can slink away without NPCs noticing you left unless your allies remind them of you. Additionally, if you return to the same location during the same scene, NPCs won't notice that you ever left.

Well Placed Contacts

You have well-placed contacts that you can rely on for information. When you succeed on a Task to gain information about what’s going on in the world beyond your immediate surroundings, your first use of the Gain Information momentum spend is free.

Pickpocket

With deft fingers, you can easily snatch items away from their owners. You can easily steal small, insignificant items without needing to make a roll. For larger or more important items that would be missed, you may choose to automatically succeed on any Task made to take the item, but the owner will notice that it’s missing.

Class Archetypes

The following are archetypes based on the social classes in the character creation that are common to settings such as Ascension’s Edhela setting.

Peasant

(Requires the Commoner [Peasant] social class)
You were born to a lower class—the farmers, the laborers, the craftsmen, the poor. It has left you with certain knowledge of the world.

Back of Your Hand

When navigating a city or region with which you are familiar, you are able to avoid implicit dangers, potentially avoiding dangerous encounters. You may attempt a Difficulty 2 Awareness + Study Task in order to use this ability in unfamiliar environments.

Folk Hero

You are greatly renowned among the common folk. Once per session, you can automatically succeed on an authority task to encourage a mob to take action, redirect their focus, or disperse.

Additionally, commonfolk who know of you will go out of their way to offer you assistance, boarding, and food.

Instantly Forgotten

Your low status makes you easily forgettable. Anyone you interact with or encounter only briefly won’t remember your name or description well enough to describe you unless you want them to, allowing you to avoid being found later.

Master of the Trade

When you take this talent, choose a single of your focuses that relates to a trade or craft of some kind. Once per session, when you spend your Determination on a Task where this Focus applies, you may instantly get it back after the roll.

Merchant

(Requires the Commoner [Merchant] social class.)

You may be low born, but are well off and educated, and have social privileges the peasants do not.

Merchant Solidarity

Once per scene, you can appeal to your status as a common merchant to appeal to another merchant to automatically succeed on a task trying to get information or assistance from them.

Populo Grosso

Your wealth grants you a certain amount of respect across all social classes. Creating an Advantage costs 1 less Momentum when using it to help you with Tasks to interact with someone whose social class is above yours.

Verified Expert

Your skill in your trade has given you a vast amount of expertise in the matter. You may always apply your social class to create a discounted advantage for study tasks that you have an applicable focus for.

In My Employ

When another character that is employed by you or serving you attempts a Task, you may spend your Determination in order to grant its effects to that character. When you do this, you also create an Advantage for yourself related to the task.

High Born

(Requires the Petty Nobility, Landed Nobility, or Royalty social class)

You are an important person, and everyone knows it. Your opinions are destined to shape the land, so others treat you differently.

Of Want to Please

People want to get on your good side. Once per Session, you can automatically succeed on any Diplomacy task if you promise to help the target Character out in the future (you need not keep this promise, of course, but may suffer a Complication if you don’t).

Noble Privilege

You can never be accused of trespassing or breaking petty laws by anyone who isn't a noble or isn’t the direct owner of the property you are violating. Servants and the working class will assume that wherever you are and whatever you are doing, you are allowed—unless they've been told beforehand by their master to particularly look out for you.

Reputation Precedes You

You have something of a reputation and can use it to your advantage. When you attempt a Task to interact with someone you’ve never met before, you may roll two extra dice without cost, but the Complication range increases by 2. If you roll a Complication, they’ve heard of you before, but they’re not pleased by what your reputation would suggest.

Above the Law

Your status places you above the scrutiny that others might face. When you are about to be arrested or face legal consequences of some kind, you may instead take a complication and avoid immediate repercussions.

Setting Archetypes

The following are archetypes based on the kinds of people that are common to Ascension’s setting of Edhela and many medieval settings.

Carouser

If partying is an art, then you’re a maestro, an expert in having a good time and using its opportunities to your advantage.

Heavyweight

Once per scene, you may automatically succeed at a task to resist any negative effects from excessive consumption of alcohol, drugs, or other substances. Additionally, when you are drunk or similarly inebriated, the Difficulty on all diplomacy tasks against others under the influence is reduced by 1.

Life of the Party

You can channel the mood of a crowd to your advantage. You may reroll on a die on any attempt to sway an excited or partying crowd, and gain two bonus momentum on a success.

Terrible Influence

You make anything and everything seem cool and compelling if you are encouraging it. Whenever you attempt to convince another character to indulge in vice—such as drinking, substances, gambling, or sexual impropriety—they must suffer a complication if they refuse, even if you fail a relevant task.

The Party Doesn’t Start Without Me

Whenever you perform a task to attempt to join a social gathering or event that you do not have an invitation to or are not welcome in, you may always choose to succeed at cost. This may generate multiple complications if you attempt to bring others in with you, at the GM’s discretion.

Never Stop Gambling

You can’t help but chase the thrill of uncertainty and chance.  Whenever you perform a task that involves a high amount of risk, as determined by the GM, you may increase your complication range to roll an additional die. The first time you use this ability in a session the increase in complication range is 1. The increase goes up by 1 each time this ability is subsequently used in the same session (+2 on the second, +3 on the third, etc.) to a maximum range of 5.

Jester

You are a professional goofball, skilled at using your hijinks and ability to entertain to get what you want.

The Fool’s Privilege

You are not expected to be taken seriously. Once a scene, you may ignore a social complication entirely, and may ignore each further social complication by spending 1 momentum.

Defusive Humor

You know how to break the tension with jokes. Once per scene, you may reduce the cost of creating an advantage to put someone at ease by 1. Additionally, once during a negotiation task, you may automatically succeed on an Excuse or Chit-Chat task.

Master of None

When performing a task outside of combat without a focus, each additional die you purchase costs only 1 momentum.

The Entertainer’s Finesse

When you succeed in a task related to some performative skill that you have a focus in (e.g. juggling, tumbling, singing, etc.), you generate two bonus momentum that must be spent on creating a social advantage.

From the Margins

You have learned to use what makes you unique to your own advantage. If you have a trait that is considered unusual or looked down upon by your current society, you may always apply it to gain a discounted advantage on performative or persuasion tasks. Additionally, it does not give you a complication on social tasks as long as you are around close allies or friends.

Knight

Honorbound and oathsworn, you are tasked with defending the weak and upholding justice.

Chivalry

Once per session, if you spend your determination while acting to defend someone else, you immediately regain it.

Courtly Love

When you act in the name of someone who is the object of your affections, but they are not there to witness it, you generate an extra point of Momentum on a successful Task that can be spent immediately or saved to the group pool.

Bold and Brave

When you attempt a Task using Presence or Skirmish and buy one or more d20s by adding to Threat, you may re-roll a single d20 in your dice pool.

Tourney Knight

When you attempt an Opposed Task outside of combat and fail, your opponent doesn’t generate any Momentum/Threat.

Rallying Cry

When you spend your determination, you may also add 3 Momentum to the pool.

Magnate

You come from wealth, either inherited or by your own shrewd investment.

Endless Coffers

Money isn't an issue for you. Whenever you create an Advantage arising from you spending money, you may decrease the Difficulty of the task by 2 instead of 1. Additionally, you may always succeed at cost to convince someone to do something for you—such as give information, betray someone, sell you something—by paying them, so long as there was any chance of success in the first place.

Loyal Retainer

You have a loyal servant whose job is to assist you in everyday tasks—such as a secretary, a page, a squire, a maidservant, etc. They can be delegated small tasks without issue; obey your instructions, within reason; and can assist you on any tasks as deemed appropriate by the GM.

You know them well enough to judge their loyalty. You may roll an additional die on any task to ascertain if they’re lying to you, have betrayed you, or otherwise are being deceitful.

Magnanimous Patron

You do not need to spend Momentum in order to be assisted by more than one character.

Debt Collector

Whenever a character owes you a debt, material or financial, the cost to create an advantage on diplomacy tasks against them is reduced by 1 as if you had a relevant trait. Additionally, you may always succeed on such tasks against them by notably reducing or forgiving the debt.

Make it Happen

Your wealth means you are well connected into patronage networks and can easily find the best person for any job. Once a session, when you need someone for a job—a craftsman, an artist, an expert, a conman, etc.— you may ask the GM where you can find the best person for the job and what you will need to hire them. Subsequent uses during the same session cost 1 momentum.

Priest

(Requires the Acolyte career)

You are a religious figure, respected even by many not of your own faith.

Blessings Abound

1/scene, when you assist an ally using Faith, you may roll two dice.

Heavenly Authority

You speak with an authority invested in you by Heaven Itself. When you use Faith to make an Authority or Diplomacy Task, you may reroll a single d20 in your dice pool for that Task.

Of Sacred Order

You are in community with the ascetic and/or monastic members of your faith and can call on them for assistance. When you are in need of information, you may seek out answers from your fellow acolytes, who will either give you what you need or point you in the right direction. You also gain an Advantage to be used on a Task acting on information you receive.

Pillar of Salt

When someone acts against the tenets of your faith and you rebuke them, you may give them a Complication representing their status as someone in opposition to your faith, affecting all Tasks to interact with other members of your faith (it may even serve as an Advantage when interacting with fellow blasphemers). This Complication lasts until either you or the GM decides that they have sufficiently repented.

Penitent

When you humble yourself before Heaven, your humility is rewarded. When you attempt any Faith Task for which you have a focus that applies, you may choose not to use that focus. If you still succeed on the roll, you gain 2 bonus momentum that can be spent to either get rid of an existing Complication, or create a new Advantage.

Rake

(Requires Presence 9)

The allure of your charm draws folk of all kinds to you, and you know just how to take advantage of it.

String Them Along

Your seductions leave an impression. Once per session, you automatically succeed on a diplomacy task to convince someone you’ve previously romanced to help you with something, so long as you have not aggrieved them since. Further, whenever you try to appease an aggrieved lover, the Difficulty of any rolls is reduced by one.

Leave them Wanting More

Whenever you leave in the middle of a conversation, your conversation partner will be left wishing it had continued. The next time you speak to them, they’ll be more inclined to appease you and give you something you want, giving you an extra d20 in any diplomacy tasks to convince them to do what you want.

Intimate Multitasker

When you are engaged with a lover, you are able to perform a second subtle task, such as eavesdropping or pickpocketing, without their noticing and without getting distracted.

Further, whenever you are publicly engaged with a lover or lovers, any onlookers will assume your full attention is on your lovers and not on any secondary task.

All the Court’s Secrets

You are amazing at extracting information from your lovers. Whenever you successfully seduce someone, you gain two bonus momentum that must be spent on Obtain Information and may not be saved to the group pool.

Come Back to My Room

Once per session, you can use this talent to make an individual that you have successfully charmed or wooed willing to follow you to a private location in spite of any concerns for their own safety or well-being, so long as it is not obviously life-threatening.

Retainer

An artist, a servant, a philosopher. Whatever you are, you have made a life working in the service of others.

Contract Work

You rely on the patronage of others to fund your artistic and/or scholarly endeavors, and in exchange help to fill your patron's court with wonder and magnificence.

You may enter into contracts with others to give your services in exchange for funding, protection, etc. While you are under contract from your patron(s), once per scene a task made in order to fulfill your contract generates two bonus momentum, which may not be saved to the group pool.

Servant’s Gossip

Whenever you interact with a courtier, servant, or retainer, you may automatically succeed at any task to get them to share secrets and scandals about their patron, so long as it does not put them or their patron in immediate danger.

At Your Service

Whenever you assist in a task, you and the character you are assisting may each reroll a single die in the task.

Fine Reputation

You are considered a master in your field, and with that comes certain boons of networking. Any potential patron or colleague will always hear you out when you approach them, and your name will be recognized by anyone with a connection to or interest in your field.

Prospective Patronage

When attempting a Task to persuade or convince someone to hire you or pay for your services, you may add an extra die to your dice pool.

Romantic

Though the world can often be complicated and grim, it has never been able to stomp out your idealistic, dreamer’s heart.

Damsel in Distress

When others assist you on a Task, their successes always count towards the result, whether you rolled a success or not.

Diamond in the Rough

Whether as a noble disguising yourself as a commoner to avoid being recognized, or as a commoner disguising yourself as a noble to gain access to a higher status, you have mastered the art of disguise in order to get around the circumstances of your birth. When entering a scene in disguise, you gain an Advantage on all Tasks to remain unnoticed or to maintain your fake identity.

Heartsong

Once per session, when you sing for someone, you may choose to reveal one of your Values as part of your song, and you may choose one character (PC or NPC) that is listening who must reveal one of their Values to you in return.

I Believe in You!
When an ally fails a roll in which they were unassisted, you may roll a die to assist using your Faith or Presence + the requisite skill. This may only occur after the result of the roll has been declared but before the outcome has been described.

Wish Upon a Star

In addition to your Values, you have a Wish: a secret dream or desire that you helplessly yearn to fulfill. You may call upon this Wish in order to spend Determination in the same way you would use a Value or the Common Cause, though you may only do so once per session. When you spend Determination using your Wish, roll 1[CD]. If an effect is rolled, you regain that point of Determination.

Vizier

(Requires Presence 9)

You are the whisper in the king’s ear, the right hand of the crown, and the true power behind the throne.

Lull into Security

Whenever you attempt a Task to make your target relax or trust you, you gain a bonus d20. Further, you may always Succeed at Cost on these tasks, with each complication you suffer adding +1 to the Difficulty of further Tasks to maintain your target's trust and goodwill.

Like a Book

You may spend your Determination to be able to hone your ability to detect lies. For the rest of the scene, you can always tell when someone is lying to you as long as you can see their face.

The Hand

You act not in your own name, but in the name of someone greater than you. Once per session, you may ignore the effects of a Complication, instead conferring it to your liege lord.

Silver-Tongued

When you attempt a Diplomacy Task while lying, you gain one extra d20 which you can reroll.

The Devil’s Bargain

When someone else would challenge or comply with one of their Values in order to gain an extra point of Determination, you may offer them your own point of Determination instead, stopping them from doing so. If they take your bargain, you gain an Advantage to spend on your next roll. If they refuse, you keep your Determination.

Magickal Archetypes

Edhela is full of magick, and people who can do magick. These archetypes are for those individuals who wield the gifts of the arcane.

Magician

(Requires Arcane Magick)

As a Magician, you can use Arcane Magick in your everyday life.

Arcane Secrets

Whenever you attempt a Task to understand a piece of magick, you gain two Bonus Momentum which you must spend on Gather Information. You gain this bonus momentum even if you fail the Task.

Artificer

When you attempt an Extended Task to perform a spell or create an object using your Magick, you may reroll the Progress dice once without spending any momentum.

Prestidigitation

1/scene, when you choose not to roll on a Difficulty 0 Task to perform a feat of Magick, you may create a free Advantage.

Scrying
Whenever you attempt a Task using Magick + Intrigue that targets another character, you may increase the Complication range of the Task by 2 in order to gain a bonus die. If you have a possession or body part (like a lock of hair) belonging to the target of your Task, you may gain a bonus die without the Complication range increase.

Telecast

When you perform a Task to communicate with someone magickally, you may always succeed at cost.

Theurgist

(Requires Light Magick)
With enough faith and blessings from above, you channel Light Magick in all things.

Divine Healer

When you succeed on a Magick + Medicine Task, you gain 2 bonus momentum.

Intercession
You appeal to a higher power for a miracle. 1/session, when facing a Difficulty 6 Task that has not been reduced by any other effects, all dice you purchase cost 1 Momentum.

Oracle

1/session you may ask the GM about the outcome of a course of action you or another character intends to take, and the GM must give you an honest answer, choosing one of the following omens: weal, woe, weal and woe, or nothing.

Warding

When you successfully perform a Task to create a magickal protection or ward, you always know when something triggers it and when it wears off. The Difficulty on any Task to re-enable a ward you created is reduced by 1.

Will of Heaven

When an ally attempts a Task, before the roll occurs, you may choose to turn one of the dice in their pool into a 10. You may use this ability once per session.

Witch

(Requires Dark Magick)
You practice a Dark Magick, one that scrapes against the edges of the world, testing its limits…

Bargain with Darkness

Whenever you give Threat to roll extra dice on a Task using your Magick, you may reroll any number of the purchased dice once and keep either result.

Cloaked in Shadow

Your mastery of darkness allows you to maneuver unseen. You may roll an extra die on any Task you perform to remain hidden or move stealthily.

It Catches Up

1/session, when you fail a Task, you may reroll your entire dice pool. If you succeed on the second attempt, you must reroll your dice pool on the next Task that you succeed. This must be done before the outcome of the roll is determined.

Soul Read

1/session, when you succeed on a Magick + Diplomacy Task to decipher someone’s intentions, you may also feel their emotions in that moment as if they were your own. You may spend 2 Momentum to also learn the target’s surface thoughts.

The Dark Power

1/session, you may consult a Dark Power for guidance or insight. The Dark Power is not trustworthy, and the GM may be tricky or misleading when answering. If you heed the Dark Power, you gain a bonus die on your next Task, though the Complication range increases by 1. If you do not, the GM gains 1 Threat, and the Complication range of your next Task increases by 1.

Combat Talents

Each Combat Talent is presented in the following format:

TALENT FORMAT

(Talent Prerequisites)
Brief description of the Talent and how it’s used.

In the layout above, you can see how Talents branch off of each other, with some Talents sharing the same prerequisite Talent.

In this layout:

  • Talent 1 must be taken before Talents 2 and 3.
  • Talent 2 must be taken before Talent 4.
  • Talent 3 must be taken before Talent 5.

Each talent in a talent tree will then be listed with a description of their effect.

Weapon Adept Talents

SWORD ADEPT

(Requires Agility 10)
You are especially trained with the sword, and can use the weapon to its fullest potential.

Sword Adept
When you attack with a weapon that has the Sword tag, the bonus momentum cost to use Swift Task to attack again is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

Blade Master 1
If you miss an attack with a weapon with the Sword tag and take the Swift Task to attack again the same turn, you may add a bonus die to your pool on the second attack.

Blade Master 2
When you use Swift Task to make an attack with the Sword tag, lower the Difficulty on that attack’s roll by -1.

Into the Fray 1
Once a round, when you successfully defend using a weapon with the Sword tag against a melee attack, you may use a reaction to move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

Into the Fray 2
When you take the Sprint Major Action, you may also make an attack with a weapon with the Sword tag as part of this action, but only after you’ve finished your movement.

Parrying Master 1
You may perform two rerolls instead of one if you are wielding two items with the Parrying quality.

Parrying Master 2
While defending while wielding two weapons with the parrying quality, the complication range of your attacker is increased by 2.

AXE ADEPT

(Requires Brawn 10)
You are especially trained with the axe, and can use the weapon to its fullest potential.

Axe Adept

1/turn, when wielding a weapon with the Axe tag, you can reroll any number of damage dice in your pool without spending bonus momentum.

Big Swing 1
When you miss on an attack while wielding a weapon with the Axe tag, you may reroll the attack against a different target within Reach.

Big Swing 2
If you choose to attack a target you successfully attacked with a weapon with the Axe tag in the previous round, you may reduce the Difficulty of that attack by 1 (to a minimum of 0).

Crusher 1
You may spend a Minor Action to give your next attack with a weapon with the Axe tag the Knockdown damage effect.

Crusher 2
When you successfully knock an enemy Prone using a weapon with the Axe tag, you gain 1 bonus momentum.

Guarding Axe 1
When you take the Block Minor Action while wielding a weapon with the Axe tag, you may also move up to half your speed.

Guarding Axe 2
When you take the Block Minor Action while wielding a weapon with the Axe tag, you or the target gains an additional 2[CD] Temporary HP.

SPEAR ADEPT

(Requires Coordination 10)
You are especially trained with the spear, and can use the weapon to its fullest potential.

Spear Adept
1/turn when you make an attack with a weapon with the Spear tag, you may add a bonus die to your roll.

Long Reach 1
When you make a successful melee attack with a weapon with the Spear tag against a target that is not adjacent to you, you gain 1 bonus momentum.

Long Reach 2
When wielding a weapon with the Extended Quality, you may spend a Minor Action to give all melee attacks made against you +1 Difficulty until the start of your next turn. This benefit is lost if you cannot see your attacker or are prone.

Precise Piercer 1
Gain the following Minor Action:

  • Pierce: While wielding a weapon with the Spear tag with two hands or with one hand free, you may spend a Minor Action to give your next attack the Piercing quality.

Precise Piercer 2
You may roll an additional number of [CD] equal to the weapon’s base damage rating on an attack benefiting from the Pierce Minor Action.

Hold the Line 1
Whenever a character enters or takes any movement inside your Reach, you may make an Opportunity Attack against them.

Hold the Line 2
As a Minor Action while wielding a weapon with the Spear tag, you prepare yourself for an onslaught of enemies. You may use the Opportunity Attack reaction once every turn until the start of your next turn.

BOW ADEPT

(Requires Awareness 10)
You are especially trained with the bow, and can use the weapon to its fullest potential.

Bow Adept
While also wielding a weapon with the Bow tag, when you take the Aim Minor Action and reroll a die, you may choose between results.

Sniper 1
At the start of your turn, you may use a free action to become Immobilized until the start of your next turn. While Immobilized, your attacks with weapons with the Bow tag gain +3 Range.

Sniper 2
While Immobilized, you gain an extra +3[CD] on ranged attacks with weapons with the Bow tag.

Close Range Shooter 1
You ignore the Difficulty increase when making a ranged attack with a weapon with the Bow tag within the target’s Reach. If you would already have this benefit (e.g. wielding a bow with the Close Quarters quality), you gain 1 bonus momentum after a successful attack with a weapon with the Bow tag against a target if you are within their Reach.

Close Range Shooter 2
When you succeed on a defense against ranged and melee weapon attacks, you may counterstrike with a weapon with the Bow tag.

Bowmaster 1
When you make an attack with a weapon with the Bow tag benefiting from the Aim Minor Action, you may choose to give the attack the Pinning damage effect or the Burst 1 quality.

Bowmaster 2
If you miss an attack with a weapon with the Bow tag benefiting from the Aim Minor Action, you gain a bonus die on your next bow attack.

GAUNTLET ADEPT

(Requires Agility, Brawn, or Coordination 10)

For you, every battle is a fistfight.

Gauntlet Adept
You may spend a Minor Action in order to grant your next attack with a weapon weapon with the Gauntlets tag the Knockdown damage effect.

Duck and Weave 1
After making a successful attack with a weapon with the Gauntlets tag, you may move either one space directly back from your target, or you may move through their space to an adjacent tile, without provoking opportunity attacks.

Duck and Weave 2
When you make an attack with a weapon with the Gauntlets tag, successful or not, you may move up to 2 spaces away from your target, or you may move through their space to an adjacent tile and then move 1 additional space, without provoking opportunity attacks.

Mean Right Hook 1
Your attacks with weapons with the Gauntlets tag also gain Knockback 1.

Mean Right Hook 2
1/scene, you may use your Major Action to perform a Mighty Blow with a weapon with the Gauntlets tag. Make an attack, as normal. On a success, you double the amount of damage dice granted from your weapon (not the damage dice from your Skirmish), and your target gains the Dazed condition until the end of their next turn.

Unarmed Fighter 1
You may use your bare fists to attack. Your unarmed attacks are 0[CD] Gauntlet weapons (they only deal [CD] equal to your Skirmish). When you succeed on an unarmed attack, you generate 1 bonus momentum.

Unarmed Fighter 2
You may make two unarmed attacks as part of the same attack action if both hands are free.

CAVALRY ADEPT

(Requires 9 Coordination)

You are trained in cavalry combat, and are especially effective on the battlefield while mounted.

Cavalry Adept

You do not suffer the Difficulty Increase for Tasks taken while mounted in combat. If you are wielding a weapon with the Saddleback quality, you gain 1 bonus momentum after a successful mounted attack.

Mounted Combatant 1

You may spend a Minor Action to give your Saddleback weapon the Knockdown damage effect. If your weapon already has this damage effect, instead you reduce the number of [!] needed to knock your target prone by -1.

Mounted Combatant 2

When making an attack with a Saddleback weapon while mounted, you gain a bonus die.

Spur 1

Your mounted speed is increased by 3. This does not apply to flying mounts.

Spur 2

For every 3 tiles you move in a row before making a melee attack while mounted, the attack gains an extra 1[CD] damage, up to a maximum of 4[CD].

Flier 1

You are able to ride a flying mount, and may Recall your mount as a Minor Action instead of a Major one.

Flier 2

Whenever you successfully evade or counter an attack while on a flying mount, you gain 2 bonus momentum.

RAPIER ADEPT

(Requires Agility 9)

You know how to bring a rapier to the battlefield.

Rapier Adept

Before or after you make an attack with a Rapier, you may perform one additional Minor Action without needing to spend bonus momentum if your other hand is free or holding an Effortless item.

Weapon of Authority 1

When you make a successful attack with a Rapier, you may nominate a single ally within line of sight, who receives a bonus die on their next Task.

Weapon of Authority 2

After you use your Major Action to attempt a Task using Authority, the cost of using a Swift Task to attack with a Rapier is reduced by 1 bonus Momentum, to a minimum of 0.

Fencer 1

After making an attack with your Rapier, the bonus Momentum cost to perform a Swift Task to attack with it again is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

Fencer 2

When wielding a Rapier in one hand and a Dagger in the other, you may apply the Effortless quality to the Dagger. In addition, when you successfully defend against an attack from an enemy while doing so, the Difficulty of your next attack against the attack is reduced by 1.

THROWN WEAPONS ADEPT

(Requires Awareness 9)
You are uniquely trained in using thrown weapons.

Thrown Weapons Adept
When you make a successful attack with a weapon with the Thrown quality, you generate 1 bonus momentum.

Pinning Accuracy 1
Your attacks with weapons with the Thrown quality gain the Pinning damage effect.

Pinning Accuracy 2
If you Aim before making an attack with a weapon with the Thrown quality and the Pinning damage effect, the target is immobilized regardless of how many effects are rolled.

Create Some Distance 1
The range on your attack with weapons with the Thrown quality increases by 2. All weapons with the Thrown quality you wield gain an additional use before they are depleted.

Create Some Distance 2
When you take the Disengage Major Action, you may make an attack with a weapon with the Thrown quality as part of the same action. Weapons with the Thrown quality gain two further additional uses before they are depleted.

General Talents

ANTAGONIST

(Requires Diplomacy 3)
Your presence on the battlefield strikes terror in the hearts of your enemies.

Antagonist
You deal an additional +2[CD] on a successful Demoralize task.

Flag of Dread 1

When you hold a Banner, you gain 1 bonus momentum on all successful Demoralize tasks and the range of your Demoralize increases by 3.

Flag of Dread 2

While holding a Banner, your Demoralize [CD] rolls gain the Terrifying damage effect.

Taunting 1
When you use Demoralize to deal more damage than the target’s remaining Willpower, they take any leftover Willpower damage as HP Damage, ignoring Resistance.

Taunting 2
You may spend a Minor Action in order to target two enemies with your next Demoralize attack.

BANNERLORD

(Requires Presence 9)

Your presence on the battlefield inspires courage in your allies.

Bannerlord 1

You may wield a Banner without it taking up one of your hands (e.g. you can effectively fight with a Banner attached to a weapon, or to your armor), or, if wielding a Banner in one of your hands, you may reroll a die when attempting an Authority Task or using the Direct Major Action.

Bannerlord 2
When you succeed on an Authority Task while wielding a Banner or your target during the Direct Major Action is successful, you may also choose any number of allies within range equal to your Presence to receive one of the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

  • Their Speed increases by 2.
  • They gain 5 temporary HP.
  • They gain +1[CD] on all damage rolls.

Bannerlord 3
When you succeed on an Authority Task while wielding a Banner or your target during the Direct Major Action is successful, you may also choose any number of allies within range equal to your Presence to use a reaction in order to move up to their speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

BERSERKER

(Requires Brawn 10)

Every time you enter battle, a red haze falls over your eyes. It dulls the senses and quiets the mind, and when it passes, you often find yourself victorious, with a trail of blood and destruction left in your wake.

Berserker 1

At the start of your turn, you may spend a Minor Action to go berserk. Until you end this effect as a free action at the start of your turn, you gain a bonus die on all melee attacks and deal +2[CD] damage on a successful attack. While berserk, you can not regain HP or WP, and all attacks against you gain a bonus die.

Berserker 2

You gain +2 speed while berserk, and your attacks gain the Terrifying damage effect.

Berserker 3

While berserk, all damage dealt to you is halved, and you gain a bonus die to defend against Demoralize Tasks.

BUCKLER MASTER

(Requires Skirmish 4)

You know how to use a small but simple shield to its full effect.

Buckler Master 1

Your buckler counts as a weapon with the Gauntlet tag that deals 1[CD] Stunning damage.

Buckler Master 2

You can use your buckler to make an opening in your target’s defenses. You may spend a Minor Action while wielding a buckler to decrease the Difficulty of your next attack with a different weapon by 1. Your buckler then loses the Parrying quality until the start of your next turn.

Buckler Master 3

You may keep the Parrying quality after using your buckler to create an opening.

COMBAT MEDIC

(Requires Medicine 3)

Where others throw themselves into battle to hurt people, you do it to help them.

Combat Medic

Whenever you attempt the First Aid Task during combat, you gain a bonus d20.

Healing Hands 1

You gain 1 bonus momentum on a successful First Aid task.

Healing Hands 2

When you make a successful First Aid Task, you roll [CD] equal to twice your Medicine Skill.

Field Doctor 1

When you attempt the First Aid Task, you may also remove a single negative Status affecting the target.

Field Doctor 2

After making a successful First Aid Task, you may choose to have you or the target of your First Aid Task move up to their speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

COMMANDER

(Requires Authority 3)

You are skilled in the art of command.

Commander

You gain access to the Direct Major Action. When you take the Direct or Issue Orders Major Actions, you automatically generate 1 bonus momentum to spend on your turn.

Mastermind 1

2/scene, when an ally attempts a Task, you may use your reaction to allow them to reroll all dice in their pool, but they must use the second result.

Mastermind 2

1/round, when an ally within line of sight attempts a Task, you may use a reaction to Assist with your Presence + Authority.

Bark Orders 1
When you Direct an ally, they may reroll a single die in their pool when attempting the Task as part of that Direct.

Bark Orders 2
When you Direct an ally, they may perform a single Minor Action in addition to their Major Action. This may be done in either order.

CLOSE PROTECTION

When you keep your allies close, you keep them safe.

Close Protection 1

When you take the Guard Action to protect someone else, until the start of your next turn, any time they move, you may move up to your speed maintaining adjacency to them. This does not apply to involuntary movement, and any movement you take in this way provokes opportunity attacks as normal.

Close Protection 2

When you take the move action on your turn, you may choose a willing adjacent ally to move with you. They may move up to their speed while remaining adjacent to you, and their movement does not trigger opportunity attacks, though your movement may.

Close Protection 3

1/round when an adjacent ally is targeted by an attack, you may use your reaction to swap places with them, making yourself the target of the attack instead.

DEFENSIVE STANCE

Sometimes the best offense is a good defense.

Defensive Stance 1

At the start of your turn, you may take a Defensive Stance as a Minor Action. While in a defensive stance, you gain 5 temporary HP that lasts until the start of your next turn or until depleted.

Defensive Stance 2

While in a defensive stance, you may choose between Agility, Brawn, or Coordination instead of the attack’s default Attribute whenever you would make an Opposed Task to defend yourself against a melee attack.

Defensive Stance 3

While in a Defensive stance, all attacks made against you gain +1 Difficulty until the start of your next turn, but all your attacks also increase in Difficulty by +1.

DEFENSIVE WALL

You are the wall standing between death and your allies.

Defensive Wall 1
After you take the Guard Major Action while wearing armor, you gain 1 bonus momentum.

Defensive Wall 2
Whenever you take the Guard Major Action while wearing armor, the Difficulty is reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 0).

Defensive Wall 3
While wearing armor, while taking actions, using abilities, or creating effects that depend on adjacency to your allies, all allies within Range 2 of you count as adjacent.

DEMORALIZING ATTACKER

(Requires Presence 10)

In the thick of battle, your words have an edge as sharp as your blade.

Demoralizing Attacker 1
Your attacks cut at your foes’ will to fight. Gain the following Minor Action:

  • Willbreaker: As a Minor Action, you give your next attack the Daunting 1 damage effect.

Demoralizing Attacker 2
Attacks you make against Characters with no Willpower gain +2[CD].

Demoralizing Attacker 3
Willbreaker gives the Daunting 2 damage effect instead of Daunting 1.

DIRTY FIGHTER

(Requires Intrigue 3)

The rules of honorable combat are for cowards. You know better.

Dirty Fighter

Your first successful attack against an enemy in an encounter also inflicts the Slowed status until the end of the target’s next turn.

Tricky Fighter 1

Gain the following Minor Action:

  • Fiendish: As a Minor Action, you give your next attack Knockback 2.

Tricky Fighter 2

When you use the Fiendish Minor Action, your next attack also gains the Pinning damage effect.

Dogpile 1

If a character within your Reach is attacked by one of your allies, you can make an Opportunity Attack against this target as a reaction.

Dogpile 2

If you attack an opponent who has been successfully attacked by one of your allies in the past round, you gain a bonus d20 on your attack roll.

DUAL WIELDING

(Requires Brawn 10 or Agility 10)

You have trained to wield two weapons at once.

Dual Wielding

After making an attack, the bonus momentum cost to perform a Swift Task to attack with a different weapon is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0. When dual wielding, one or both of the weapons being wielded must be 1H, and the character must choose which weapon they are attacking with before making the roll for the Task.

Double Blow 1

1/scene when wielding two weapons with the Axe tag at once, as a Major Action you may strike with both in one powerful attack, rolling to hit only once but dealing the damage of both weapons. You may not perform a Swift Task this turn.

Double Blow 2

When you defeat an enemy using Double Blow 1, you gain a bonus die on your next attack.

Whirlwind 1

When wielding two weapons with the Sword tag, you may spend a Minor Action to give your next attack the Burst 1 quality.

Whirlwind 2

When wielding two weapons with the Sword tag, you may spend your Determination to use the Attack action to make two attacks, one with each weapon. If you use a Swift Task to attack again on the same turn, you may attack twice more, once with each weapon.

DUELIST

You do best in single combat.

Duelist 1

1/scene, as a Minor Action you may challenge a single enemy within line of sight on the battlefield to a duel, giving them Duelist’s Mark. While an enemy has Duelist’s Mark, you gain 2 bonus momentum on successful melee attacks against them, but +1 Difficulty on attacks against any other target. Duelist’s Mark lasts until the marked enemy is defeated, or until you drop the mark as a free action at the beginning of your turn.

Duelist 2

An enemy marked with Duelist’s Mark can’t voluntarily move away from you and you can’t voluntarily move away from them, unless either of you takes the disengage Major Action.

Duelist 3

Enemy marked with Duelist’s Mark gain +1 Difficulty on attacks against targets other than you. Additionally, when an enemy with Duelist’s Mark is defeated, you may immediately apply it to a new target within line of sight as a free action.

FEINT

(Requires Intrigue 3)
You deceive your opponents to create an opening.

Feint 1
Gain the following Minor Action:

  • Feint: As a Minor Action, you declare a Feint against a target. Your next melee attack against them uses Intrigue instead of Skirmish for calculating your target number and the attack’s damage. Your target must do the same or you gain a bonus die on the attack.

Feint 2
When you take the Feint Minor Action, you may also replace your weapon’s base damage with [CD] equal to your Intrigue on your next attack.

Feint 3
You may Feint as a Free Action if an ally is adjacent to the target.

FORTIFIED MIND

(Requires Faith 10)

It takes more than a little shouting to shake your resolve.

Fortified Mind 1

When targeted by a Demoralize Task, you may reroll a single die in your dice pool to defend against it.

Fortified Mind 2

Your Willpower maximum increases by +3.

Fortified Mind 3

1/round, when targeted by a Demoralize Task, you may reduce the damage by an amount equal to your Skirmish as a reaction.

HEAVY LIFTING

(Requires Brawn 10)

The power behind your blows is enough to crush anyone and everyone that crosses your path.

Heavy Lifting 1

You ignore the increase in Difficulty when wielding a two-handed weapon in one hand.

Heavy Lifting 2

Gain the following Minor Action:

  • Demolish: As a Minor Action, you grant your next attack the Burst 1 damage effect.

Heavy Lifting 3

Your Heavy weapons gain Reliable 3. In addition, when you take the Demolish Minor Action, your attack also gains the Destructive damage effect.

HELPING HAND

Your best asset is to be an asset.

Helping Hand 1
When you use the Assist Major Action, you immediately gain two Bonus Momentum to spend during your Turn.

Helping Hand 2
When you use the Assist Major Action, the assisted character may re-roll one die.

Helping Hand 3
When you use the Assist Major Action, you may roll two dice instead of one on your Assist.

HUNTER SEEKER

(Requires Awareness 10)

No one stays hidden from you for long…

Hunter Seeker 1
You may add your Skirmish to your Awareness when calculating the range for the Search Major Action.

Hunter Seeker 2
1/scene, as a free action you may choose a single enemy unit within line of sight to mark as the target of your hunt, marking them as your Quarry. While an enemy is marked as your quarry, the Difficulty of any Search actions to find them is lowered by 1, and once per attack, you may reroll any number of [CD] in your pool without spending bonus Momentum when dealing damage after a successful attack against your quarry.

Hunter Seeker 3
Enemies marked as quarry cannot benefit from the Invisible condition when attacking or defending against you. Additionally, you may take the Search Action as a Minor Action on your turn.

ICON

(Requires Authority 3)
Your inspiring presence keeps your allies in the fight.

Icon
You may use Console as a Minor Action.

Flag of Victory 1
When you hold a banner, the range of your Console Tasks increases by 3 and you can target up to 2 Characters when you Console.

Flag of Victory 2
All characters within range equal to your Authority have a bonus d20 when defending against Demoralize Tasks, and they gain Willpower equal to your Authority when they start their turn within this range.

Reassurance 1
When you successfully use Console to restore an ally’s Willpower, you may also restore your own Willpower for an amount equal to your Authority.

Reassurance 2
When you successfully Console an ally, you may also remove one non-self-inflicted Status or Condition afflicting them. Rattled cannot be removed in this way.

IMPENETRABLE

(Requires Skirmish 4)

When in battle, no one gets past you without your permission.

Impenetrable 1
Foes trigger opportunity attacks from you even when they take the Disengage Major Action.

Impenetrable 2
When you hit a target with an opportunity attack, you may also Immobilize them until the start of their next turn.

Impenetrable 3
When you Immobilize a target, you may also move them 1 tile in any direction.

INSURMOUNTABLE

You are an immovable object.

Insurmountable 1
