Enemies have +1 Difficulty when attempting to Grapple you. You have -1 Difficulty on Tasks to escape a grapple.

Insurmountable 2
You gain access to the Stand Firm Reaction:

  • Stand Firm: 1/round, as a Reaction, when an attack or hazard would knock you Prone, you may ignore it and stay standing.

Insurmountable 3
You may use the Stand Firm Reaction to ignore Forced Movement and stay in place. If an attack would knock you Prone and force you to move, you may use Stand Firm to ignore both.

JUGGERNAUT

You are an unstoppable force.

Juggernaut 1
When you succeed on a Shove action, you may move the target up to 3 spaces instead of 1.

Juggernaut 2
When you successfully Shove an enemy and push them into an obstacle that stops their movement, you may deal 3[CD] damage to them.

Juggernaut 3
Your successful Shove actions deal [CD] damage equal to your Skirmish. Additionally, when you succeed on a Shove action, you may move with the target you shove to remain adjacent to them as part of the same action.

MAGE’S BANE

Magic is the coward’s weapon, and you hate cowards.

Mage’s Bane 1

When an enemy casts a spell, you may use a reaction to make an Opportunity Attack against them if they are within Reach, or move up to your full speed towards them if they are not.

Mage’s Bane 2

3/scene, you may use the Silence Major Action.

  • Silence (Range 10): Make an Opposed Task against an enemy within Range, using Presence + Diplomacy vs. the target's Awareness + Study. On a success, the target cannot cast spells until the end of their next turn.

Mage’s Bane 3

When you succeed on an Opportunity Attack as part of Mage’s Bane, you may choose to inflict one of the following effects on your target, potentially disrupting their spell: they are knocked prone, they are pushed up to 3 spaces away from you, or they are Immobilized until the end of their next turn.

OPPORTUNIST

You know how to spot an opening.

Opportunist 1
When you make an Opportunity Attack, you may reroll one of your dice, keeping the second result.

Opportunist 2
Gain the following Major Action:

  • Blockade: Until the start of your next turn, all Opportunity Attacks you make deal an additional +2[CD] damage.

Opportunist 3
When you take the Blockade Major Action, you make all Opportunity Attacks with -1 Difficulty until the start of your next turn.

OVERWHELMING

(Requires Diplomacy 4)

You demoralize your enemies with even greater efficiency.

Overwhelming 1
When you reduce an enemy’s Willpower to 0, you may also move that unit a number of spaces equal to half your Diplomacy. This counts as involuntary movement.

Overwhelming 2
When you reduce an enemy’s Willpower to 0, you may also inflict the Immobilized condition on them, which lasts until the end of their next turn or until they are no longer Rattled.

Overwhelming 3
When you attempt a Task that targets an enemy with no Willpower, the Difficulty is reduced by 1.

POISONER

(Requires Medicine 3)

You are adept at using poisons to augment your weapon attacks.

Poisoner 1

Gain the following Minor Action:

  • Poison: As a Minor Action, you apply the Persistent 2 damage effect to one of your weapons. This lasts until you successfully attack with it or until the start of your next turn.

Poisoner 2

Persistent damage from the Poison Minor Action increases to 3, and characters suffering any Persistent damage inflicted by you have +1 Difficulty on their Task to remove it.

Poisoner 3

Persistent damage from the Poison Minor Action increases to 4, and you generate 2 bonus momentum when you make a successful attack against an enemy with Persistent damage that you’ve inflicted.

PROVOCATEUR

You are especially infuriating to your enemies.

Provocateur 1
You may spend a Minor Action to give your next attack or Demoralize the Provoking damage effect.

Provocateur 2
You gain a bonus d20 against enemies that are Enraged at you.

Provocateur 3
You deal +1 [CD] damage against enemies that are Enraged at you, and reduce the damage from their attacks against you by 1.

RALLY

You inspire and coordinate your allies.

Rally 1
You gain the following Rally Minor Action which you may use 2/scene:

  • Rally: As a Minor Action, you grant one ally within line of sight a bonus die to use on a Task. Allies cannot benefit from multiple instances of this Task at once.

Rally 2
You may use the Rally action as a reaction at the start of an ally’s turn. You may use Rally a number of times per scene equal to your Authority.

Rally 3
You gain 2 additional uses of Rally. When you use Rally on an ally, they may choose to forgo the bonus die in order to gain +2 bonus momentum to use on their turn instead.

RAPPORT

Your bond is your strength.

Rapport 1
Choose one character with whom your character has a special or significant rapport. Whenever you are adjacent to them, you may take the Assist action as a Minor Action but only to support that character. You may change the target of your rapport between sessions or during narrative play, but only if it is narratively appropriate.

Rapport 2
1/round, if the character with your rapport is targeted by a hostile action, you may use your reaction to move half your speed towards them.

Rapport 3
1/round, when the character with your rapport is adjacent to you and is dealt damage, you may reduce the damage by half, and you also take an equivalent amount of damage.

RESILIENT

It’s going to take more than just a couple hits to knock you down.

Resilient 1

Your Health Bar increases by 2 (which increases your Max HP by 6).

Resilient 2

When another character would roll dice in order to restore your HP, they gain +1[CD] and may reroll any number of [CD] in their pool.

Resilient 3

When you use the Avoid Injury Determination Spend, you regain ½ your max HP.

SHIELD MASTER

(Requires Skirmish 4)

You’ve trained with shields before, and know how to use them to their fullest potential.

Shield Master

When you take the Block Minor Action while wielding an item with the Shield quality, you gain +2 temporary HP when an effect is rolled instead of +1.

Shield Bash 1

You may wield any item with the Shield quality as a 1[CD] gauntlet with Knockback 1. As a Minor Action, you may ready your shield to increase this to Knockback 2.

Shield Bash 2

When you ready your shield, your shield's attack also gains the Stunning damage effect.

Shield Wall 1

1/round, when an adjacent ally is targeted by an attack while you are wielding an item with the Shield quality, as a reaction you may assist them on their defense roll with your Agility, Brawn, or Coordination + Skirmish.

Shield Wall 2

Any item you wield with the Shield quality gains the Effortless quality. Once per round you may reroll the extra die your shield grants.

Additionally, 1/scene while you are wielding a shield and you are hit by an attack, you may destroy your shield to ignore all damage/effects from the attack.

SKIRMISHER

You are quick into battle and quick to get out of it.

Skirmisher 1
When an opponent attacks you using an Opportunity Attack, you may inflict damage if you win the contested check.

Skirmisher 2
1/round, when an opponent targets you with an attack, you may use a reaction to make a melee attack against them first which occurs before their attack is resolved. If you miss, your opponent does not deal any damage.

Skirmisher 3
1/round, you may cause an attack taken against you as a reaction to automatically miss. This must be declared before any dice for the attack are rolled.

SLEEPYTIME

You are especially practiced at the careful art of laying your enemies flat on their backs.

Sleepytime 1

You may spend a Minor Action to apply the Stunning damage effect to your next melee attack.

Sleepytime 2

When you make a successful attack with a weapon that has the Knockdown damage effect, you automatically knock your opponent Prone, regardless of [!] rolled.

Sleepytime 3

You gain an extra d20 against Prone or Immobilized opponents.

STEALTHY FIGHTER

(Requires Intrigue 3)

You are especially adept at using stealth to take advantage of the battlefield chaos.

Stealthy Fighter 1

1/turn, after you successfully take the Attack action, you may Hide as a Minor Action.

Stealthy Fighter 2

When you make an attack while hidden, you may choose to apply one of the following effects to the target: Knockdown, Startling, or Terrifying.

Stealthy Fighter 3

When you use Stealthy Fighter 2, you may choose two effects instead of one.

SWIFT STEPS

(Requires Agility 10)

You move through the battlefield, quick and light as a feather.

Swift Steps 1
When you take the Sprint Action while unmounted, you may reduce the Bonus Momentum cost of Swift Task on the same turn by 1, to a minimum of 0.

Swift Steps 2
While unmounted, you ignore the effects of difficult terrain, and moving while Prone costs 2 speed per tile of movement, instead of 3.

Swift Steps 3
While unmounted, you may take the Move Minor Action twice each turn.

TACTICIAN

(Requires Study 3)

You have studied the art of command.

Tactician

You gain 2 bonus momentum after taking the Pinpoint Major Action. You also gain access to the Direct Major Action.

Spotter 1
When you Pinpoint an enemy, you may force them to make an opposed Task with their Reason/Study vs. your Reason/Study. On a success, you may afflict them with one of the following effects:

  • The target is Exposed until the start of their next turn.
  • The next successful attack made against the target gains +2[CD].
  • The next attack made against the target may reroll one of the dice in their pool.

Spotter 2
When using the Direct Action or issuing an army Order, you may use Reason instead of Presence. You also gain an additional effect to choose from when using Spotter 1:

  • The next successful attack made against the target also deals WP damage equal to half of the damage rolled.

Studied Combatant 1

Once a round, as a Minor Action, you can learn one of the following things about a single enemy within line of sight: their attributes and skills scores, their speed, or their current HP and current resistance.

Studied Combatant 2

When you use the Studied Combatant Minor Action, you learn all three options instead of choosing one. In addition, you may use this ability as a reaction when an enemy finishes their turn within your line of sight, but still are limited to using it once a round.

TRAPPER

(Requires Intrigue 3)

Your enemy better watch their step…

Trapper 1
3/scene, you can set one of the following traps for an enemy. As a Minor Action, you can choose a tile you can see within a range equal to your Awareness and set a trap there that lasts until triggered or the end of the scene. This trap is undetectable to enemies unless they succeed on a Search Major Action to discover it.

  • Spring Trap: When an enemy unit enters the space containing a Spring Trap, they are knocked back 4 spaces in a direction of your choice.
  • Steel Trap: When an enemy unit enters the space containing a Steel Trap, they are Immobilized until the end of their next turn.
  • Net Trap: When an enemy unit enters the space containing a Net Trap, they are ensnared, and cannot take any actions until they or an ally spends their Major Action to escape the trap, though they may continue moving if they have any movement remaining.

Trapper 2
You can set a number of traps per scene equal to twice your Intrigue, and may set two traps at a time as part of one Minor Action.

Trapper 3
When an enemy triggers one of your traps, they also take a number of [CD] damage equal to your Intrigue.

UNARMORED MASTER

(Requires Agility 10)
You work best unencumbered.

Unarmored Master 1
When you successfully defend against an attack while not wearing armor or wielding a shield or buckler, you generate 2 bonus momentum.

Unarmored Master 2
While not wearing armor or wielding a shield or buckler, you can stand from prone as part of the Move Minor Action using half your movement. In addition, your Speed is increased by 2.

Unarmored Master 3
While not wearing armor or wielding a shield or buckler, 1/round you may use a reaction to impose +1 Difficulty on an attack made against you. In addition, your Speed is increased by 3 instead of 2.

VENGEFUL

Your preferred method of fighting is waiting for your enemy to show their hand before retaliating.

Vengeful

When you successfully attack an opponent who has damaged you during the current round, you generate 2 bonus momentum.

Desperation 1
When you have at least one wound, the first attack you make on your turn deals an additional +2 Willpower damage to your opponent.

Desperation 2
When you have two wounds, the first attack you make on your turn deals an additional +3[CD].

Retribution 1
When you successfully attack an opponent who has damaged you or one of your allies during the current round, you may reroll 3[CD] without cost.

Retribution 2
Once per round, when one of your allies is successfully hit by an attack, you may use a reaction to move up to your speed and make an attack against the attacker.

WAR HEALER

(Requires Medicine 3)
Wielding a weapon doesn’t mean you can’t also heal.

War Healer 1
When you take the First Aid Major Action, the bonus Momentum cost to perform a Swift Task to make an attack on the same turn is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0.

War Healer 2
Once per round, when you make a successful attack, you may heal an adjacent ally for an amount equal to your Medicine.

War Healer 3
Once per round, when you use an action or ability to heal an ally, you may also regain HP equal to half of what your ally regained.

WILLING SHIELD

You know that death comes for everyone on the battlefield, but not them. You won't let it. If the target of your Willing Shield dies, any and all of your Willing Shield talents are replaced with their Disgraced Shield counterparts. (You may also choose to start with Disgraced Shield talents as part of your character’s backstory)

Willing Shield 1

Once per session, before entering combat, you may choose one of your allies. Once per round, when that ally within your Reach is targeted by an attack, as a reaction you may assist them on their defense roll with your Weapon’s Attribute + Skirmish.

Willing Shield 2

If you use Willing Shield to assist your targeted ally but the attacker succeeds anyways, your ally reduces the damage of the attack by 2.

Willing Shield 3

1/scene, when you use Willing Shield to assist an adjacent ally and the attacker succeeds anyways, you may take the attack instead, suffering any damage and additional effects.

Disgraced Shield 1

Once per session, you must choose one of your allies. Once per round, when that ally is successfully attacked while they are adjacent to you, you may use a reaction to shield them by taking the attack instead, suffering any damage and additional effects in their place.

Disgraced Shield 2

After using the Disgraced Shield reaction, on your next turn, your attacks against the attacker that triggered the reaction gain +2[CD]. If you use a Swift Task to attack this opponent, your bonus momentum cost to do so is reduced to 1.

Disgraced Shield 3

If you use Disgraced Shield to take an attack that would cause you to drop to 0HP, you may ignore the attack’s damage. You may do this once per combat. In addition, if you use Disgraced Shield to take an attack that reduces you to 0HP and you choose to die, you gain a bonus die on all Tasks you attempt during your final Turn.

WRESTLER

You’re not afraid to get hands-on with your opponents.

Wrestler 1

When you attempt the Grapple Major Action, you may roll using either Brawn, Agility, or Coordination as your Attribute. The target of your grapple defends using the same Attribute.

Wrestler 2

You gain a bonus die when attacking a target who is grappled. Additionally, you can use reactions while grappling an opponent.

Wrestler 3
When you make a successful melee attack against a character, you may attempt to Grapple them as a Minor Action.

Magick Talents

ARCANE MAGICK

(Requires Reason 10)

You have unlocked the secrets of Arcane Magick - a domain of magick that seeks to reveal the mysteries of the world through reliable models and experimentation.

Arcane Magick 1
You are a Spellcaster of the Arcane Domain, and can prepare Tier 1 spells from the Arcane Domain. Reason is your Magick Attribute for Arcane Spells and other Magick tasks using Arcane.

Arcane Magick 2
You can prepare Tier 2 spells from the Arcane domain. Tier 1 Arcane spells that you prepare gain 1 additional use per scene; if this would bring the uses per scene to 4 or higher, instead you may use that spell without limit.

Arcane Magick 3
You can prepare Tier 3 spells from the Arcane domain. Tier 2 Arcane spells that you prepare gain 1 additional use per scene.

DARK MAGICK

(Requires Presence 10)

You have gained the blasphemous power of Dark Magick - a domain of magick that deals with shadows, death, and blood. The Dark Arts are reviled by most, but a study in them reveals potential to change the world in ways thought impossible.

Dark Magick 1
You are a Spellcaster, and can prepare Tier 1 spells from the Dark Domain. Presence is your Magick Attribute for Dark Spells and other Magick tasks using Dark.

Dark Magick 2
You can prepare Tier 2 spells from the Dark domain. Tier 1 Dark spells that you prepare gain 1 additional use per scene; if this would bring the uses per scene to 4 or higher, instead you may use that spell without limit.

Dark Magick 3
You can prepare Tier 3 spells from the Dark domain. Tier 2 Dark spells that you prepare gain 1 additional use per scene.

LIGHT MAGICK

(Requires Faith 10)

You are blessed with the miraculous power of Light Magick - a domain of magick said to come from the divine forces that breathe life into every being. You are a conduit, a vessel for the will of something greater than any single being.

Light Magick 1
You are a Spellcaster, and can prepare Tier 1 spells from the Light Domain. Faith is your Magick Attribute for Light Spells and other Magick tasks using Light.

Light Magick 2
You can prepare Tier 2 spells from the Light domain. Tier 1 Light spells that you prepare gain 1 additional use per scene; if this would bring the uses per scene to 4 or higher, instead you may use that spell without limit.

Light Magick 3
You can prepare Tier 3 spells from the Light domain. Tier 2 Light spells that you prepare gain 1 additional use per scene.

AURATURGE

(Requires Spellcaster)

Auras are a magickal manifestation most associated with the saints of old, who had a presence of grace that emboldened the faithful.

Auraturge 1
You project your divine emanations at greater distance. Increase the Range of all Aura spells you prepare by 1 (e.g., Range 2 becomes Range 3).

Auraturge 2
If you have at least 1 Aura spell prepared, the spell slot cost for one other Aura spell is reduced by 1 (to a minimum of 1).

Auraturge 3
Your mastery allows your aura's influence to become truly pervasive. Increase the Range of all Aura spells you prepare by an additional 1. This bonus stacks with Auraturge I, granting a total Range increase of 2.

COUNTERSPELL

(Requires Spellcaster)

On the battlefield, your magick is your shield against blade and spell alike.

Counterspell 1
You gain a bonus die to defend against spell attacks when not wielding a shield or wearing armor. You may reroll this die, but must use the second result.

Counterspell 2
1/round, when an ally in line of sight is targeted by an attack spell, you may use a reaction to grant them a bonus die to defend against it.

Counterspell 3
When you or an ally that you’ve granted a bonus die to succeeds on a Task to defend against a spell attack, you may deal [CD] damage equal to your Study to the enemy that cast the spell.

CRYOMANCER

(Requires Spellcaster)

Cold is one of the fundamental energies, opposed by flame. As a Cryomancer you have an expertise in wielding bitter cold against your enemies.

Cryomancer 1
As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the Ice Tag:

  • Encasing Ice: If the target becomes Slowed by your spell, they also become Immobilized until the end of their next turn.
  • Frostbite: If the target would become Slowed by your spell, they do not - rather, they become Off-Guard until the end of their next turn.
  • Brittle Ice: If the target becomes Slowed by your spell, they also become Exposed until the end of their next turn.

Cryomancer 2
You reduce the damage from attacks with the Ice tag by -2. In addition, 1/scene when you cast an Ice spell on your turn, you may choose to first emit a burst of ice from yourself, creating a Blast 2 area of difficult terrain around yourself that you ignore and that lasts until the end of your next turn.

Cryomancer 3
2/scene, you may spend a Minor Action to apply one of the following effects to your next spell with the Ice tag:

  • Permafrost: If the target becomes Slowed by your spell, the duration of the Slowed Status lasts 1 additional round.
  • Hypothermia: If the target would become Slowed by your spell, they also become Off-Guard until the end of their next turn.
  • Shattering Ice: If the target becomes Slowed by your spell, they also become Exposed until the end of their next turn, and any attacks made against them deal an additional 2[CD] damage.

FULGERMANCER

(Requires Spellcaster)

Lightning is one of the fundamental energies, once thought to be exclusive to the skies, now conjurable with arcane understanding. As a fulgermancer you have an expertise in wielding the awesome power of thunder and lightning.

Fulgermancer 1
As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the Lightning Tag:

  • Arcing Bolt: The spell’s attack gains Burst 1.
  • Distant Spark: The spell's Range increases by 2. For spells with a Line Area originating from Self, this increases the Line length by 2
  • Static Vulnerability: If the target becomes Off-Guard from your spell, they also become Exposed until the end of their next turn.

Fulgermancer 2
You reduce the damage from attacks with the Lightning tag by -2. In addition, 1/scene when you cast a Lightning spell on your turn, you may choose to first momentarily take the form of Lightning. You teleport up to 3 spaces. Draw a straight line from where you teleported from - each character in that line takes 3[CD] Piercing 2 damage.

Fulgermancer 3
2/scene, you may spend a Minor Action to apply one of the following effects to your next spell with the Lightning tag:

  • Chain Lightning: The spell’s attack gains Burst 2.
  • Far Strike: The spell's Range increases by 4. For spells with a Line Area originating from Self, this increases the Line length by 4
  • System Shock: If the target becomes Off-Guard from your spell, they also become Exposed until the end of their next turn, and any attacks made against them deal an additional 2[CD] damage.

GREMORIE

(Requires Spellcaster)

There is power in the written word, and you know it better than anyone. Whether it be by carrying arcane tomes filled with formulae and geometry, hallowed texts of psalms and saintly philosophy, or profane curses and sigils, you can use these magick writings to their fullest potential.

Gremorie 1
Each Tome you have equipped provides 3 Spell Slots, rather than 2. Additionally, if you are holding a Tome and no other item, you do not suffer the Difficulty increase for spellcasting without a spell implement.

Gremorie 2
Once per Scene when you have a Tome equipped, as a Minor Action you can unprepare up to 3 Spell Slots worth of prepared spells, and prepare new spells by filling Spell Slots up to the number of Spell Slots you have unprepared. You cannot unprepare a spell that you have already spent uses of in this scene, if the spell has a limited number of uses.

Gremorie 3
When you Cast a spell while having a Tome equipped, you can fuel that spell using the unspent written words you are carrying. Choose up to 3 Spell Slots worth of spells that you have prepared and not spent any limited uses of in this scene - those spells become unprepared, and you gain a Bonus d20 on the Spellcasting Task for each Spell Slot unprepared in this way.

HEMOCRAFT

(Requires Spellcaster)

Blood is the medium of life in living things, and you know its secrets. A blasphemous domain of research, you may use your mastery of blood to spread disease and cure disease alike.

Hemocraft 1
As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the Blood Tag:

  • Blood Sense: The spell’s range increases by 1.
  • Diseased Blood: If the spell has the Persistent X damage effect, it becomes Persistent X +1.
  • Open Veins: On a successful hit, all Tasks to heal the target gain +1 Difficulty until the start of their next turn.

Hemocraft 2
You reduce the damage from attacks with the Blood tag by -2. 1/scene when you cast a Blood spell on your turn, you can lay a curse on the blood of those near you. All characters within Range 2 of you suffer the Persistent 3 damage effect.

Hemocraft 3
2/scene, you may spend a Minor Action to apply one of the following effects to your next spell with the Blood tag:

  • Blood Hunter: The spell’s range increases by 3.
  • Cursed Blood: If the spell inflicts the Persistent X damage effect, the target suffers +1 Difficulty to their next task to end the effect.
  • Bleeding Out: On a successful hit, the target cannot regain HP until the end of their next turn.

LUMINURGE

(Requires Spellcaster)

The Light that a blessed priest can conjure is unlike any other magickal light - the same life giving energy that Sun shines upon the land. As a luminurge, you are blessed to wield this awesome raw power as a sword and shield against your foes.

Luminurge 1

As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the Radiant Tag:

  • Dazzling Flash: On a successful hit, the target becomes Off-Guard until the end of their next turn.
  • Weakening Glare: On a successful hit, the target becomes Weakened until the end of their next turn.
  • Exposing Glint: On a successful hit, the target becomes Exposed until the end of their next turn.

Luminurge 2
You reduce the damage from attacks with the Radiant tag by -2. In addition, 1/scene when you cast a Radiant spell on your turn, you can choose to first invoke a sanctuary flair from yourself. You and allies of your choice within Range 2 of you gain +1 temporary Resistance until the start of your next turn.

Luminurge 3
2/scene, you may spend a Minor Action to apply one of the following effects to your next spell with the Radiant tag:

  • Blinding Flash: On a successful hit, the target becomes Blinded until the end of their next turn.
  • Debilitating Ray: On a successful hit, the target becomes Weakened and Off-Guard until the end of their next turn.
  • Revealed Truth: On a successful hit, the target becomes Exposed until the end of their next turn, and any attacks made against them deal an additional 2[CD] damage.

NOCTOCRAFT

(Requires Spellcaster)

The night is the absence of the life-giving light of the sun, and this is where you best dwell. Shadow-magick is the energy of death, and is mightiest when its user allows themself to be close to that threshold.

Noctocraft 1
As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the Shadow Tag:

  • Enfeebling Shroud: On a successful hit, the next Demoralize against the target deals +2[CD] damage.
  • Grip of Terror: On a successful hit, the target becomes Frightened until the end of their next turn.
  • Last Will: The spell deals +1[CD] if you have at least one Wound.

Noctocraft 2
You reduce the WP cost of Shadow spells by 1. In addition, 1/scene when you cast a Shadow spell on your turn, you create a veil of darkness around yourself. Until the end of your next turn, all Characters become Blinded while they are adjacent to you (this effect ends when they move away), and Ranged attacks against you gain +1 Difficulty.

Noctocraft 3
2/scene, you may spend a Minor Action to apply one of the following effects to your next spell with the Shadow tag:

  • Blackened Veil: On a successful hit, the target cannot regain WP until the end of their next turn.
  • Grip of Death: On a successful hit, the target becomes Frightened and Weakened until the end of their next turn.
  • Last Testament: The spell deals +3[CD] if you have at least one Wound.

PYROMANCER

(Requires Spellcaster)

Fire is said to be the first fundamental energy tamed by the ancient wizards. It is a more primal magick, spreading and growing with a life of its own. As a pyromancer, you have a knack for controlling the most fearsome flames.

Pyromancer 1
As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the fire Tag:

  • Spreading Flames: If the spell has an Area of Effect, it increases by 1.
  • Vicious Flames: The spell deals an additional 2[CD] damage.
  • Distant Flames: The spell’s range increases by 2.

Pyromancer 2
You reduce the damage from attacks with the Fire tag by -2. In addition, 1/scene when you cast a Fire spell on your turn, you can choose to first emit a burst of fire from yourself, dealing 3[CD] Piercing damage to all Characters within 1 space of yourself.

Pyromancer 3
2/scene, you may spend a Minor Action to apply one of the following effects to your next spell with the Fire tag:

  • Spreading Inferno: If the spell has an Area of Effect, it increases by 2.
  • Vicious Inferno: The spell deals an additional 3[CD] damage.
  • Distant Inferno: The spell’s range increases by 4.

SHADOW CLOAK

(Requires Spellcaster)

Using magick to make yourself invisible is a nasty, dishonorable trick - the magick of thieves and rogues. You are a master of this art.

Shadow Cloak 1
Whenever you become Invisible, you may immediately Hide as a free action.

Shadow Cloak 2
While Invisible, you gain a bonus to your Speed equal to half your Intrigue.

Shadow Cloak 3
1/turn, while Invisible, you may Teleport a number of spaces equal to your Intrigue as a free action.

SPELLBLADE

(Requires Spellcaster)
You have learned to channel your Magick through a weapon, to devastating effect.

Spellblade 1
At the start of a scene, choose a single Sword, Spear, or Axe weapon you have equipped to be your Spellblade Weapon. As long as you are holding your Spellblade Weapon with at least 1 hand, you do not suffer the Difficulty Increase of performing Magick Tasks without a Spell Implement. Additionally, you may use Magick in place of the weapon’s normal attribute for Attacking with.

Spellblade 2
Melee attacks enhanced by your Spellblade Spells gain the Piercing quality.

Spellblade 3
1/turn, you can cast a Spellblade Spell as a free action rather than a Minor Action.

SPELLSHOT

(Requires Spellcaster)

You have learned to channel your Magick through a ranged weapon.

Spellshot 1
As long as you are holding a ranged weapon with at least 1 hand, you do not suffer the Difficulty Increase of performing Magick Tasks without a Spell Implement. Additionally, your Spellblade spells can apply to ranged weapons in addition to melee weapons.

Spellshot 2
Your magically imbued arrows are able to take curved paths. When you take the Aim Minor Action, your next ranged weapon attack ignores the Difficulty increase provided by Half Cover.

Spellshot 3
You are able to effortlessly weave magick into your arrows. 1/turn, when you take the Aim Minor Action you may also Cast a Spellblade spell as a Free Action.

THYMOCRAFT

(Requires Spellcaster)

One of the most reviled acts of dark magick is to twist and drain energy from someone’s immortal soul. As a practitioner of thymocraft your magick reaches directly past the body to harm their very essence, fueling your own.

Thymocraft 1
As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the Soul Tag:

  • Weakening Drain: On a successful hit, the target becomes Weakened until the end of their next turn.
  • Lethargic Drain: On a successful hit, the target becomes Slowed until the end of their next turn.
  • Thirsting Drain: If you restore HP from the spell, you restore an additional 3 HP.

Thymocraft 2
You reduce the damage from attacks with the Soul tag by -2. In addition, 1/scene when you cast a Soul spell on your turn, you can choose to reveal a frightening ghostly aura, dealing 4[CD] Willpower damage to all Characters within 1 space of yourself.

Thymocraft 3
2/scene, you may spend a Minor Action to apply one of the following effects to your next spell with the Soul tag:

  • Will Drain: The spell’s attack gains Daunting 1.
  • Fatiguing Drain: On a successful hit, the target is also knocked prone.
  • Empowering Drain: If you restore HP from the spell, you restore an additional 5 HP and 2 WP.

VITALURGE

(Requires Spellcaster)

The power to lay on hands and mend wounds is the most well-known manifestation of divine grace. As a vitalurge, you have a great power to stop your allies from falling from their wounds.

Vitalurge 1
As a Minor Action, you may apply one of the following options to your next spell with the Healing Tag:

  • Soothing Touch: Increase the HP restored by the spell by 2.
  • Restorative Ward: The target(s) healed by the spell also gain 2 Temporary HP.
  • Cleansing Light: The target(s) healed by the spell may also clear any Persistent damage or remove one condition from the following list affecting them: Blinded, Off-Guard, Prone, Slowed, Weakened.

Vitalurge 2
1/scene when you cast a Healing spell on your turn, you can choose to first release a pulse of restorative energy. You and each ally within 1 space of you gain Temporary HP equal to your Medicine skill.

Vitalurge 3

Chapter Seven: Equipment

During an adventure, it is expected that there will be times that characters may need access to special tools, items, or other equipment that may serve their purposes. Having the right thing for the right moment can be the difference between success and failure!

Basic Equipment

Most items in Ascension do not require any sort of inventory tracking or management—outside of combat, items are used only when relevant to the action of the story, and characters may often be assumed to have basic items and supplies on them (like clothes and a traveling kit). There is no limit to the number of items a character can have, other than what the GM deems as reasonable. A character likely can’t carry a stove everywhere they go, but could reasonably fit a small cookpot in their pack.

Acquiring Items

During non-combat scenes, occasionally a player may want to acquire a specific item in order to help them with a Task. In cases like these, characters may spend 2 Momentum to Create an Advantage, with the Advantage representing the acquired item and lowering the Difficulty of the relevant Task it is needed for.

Lorenz is trying to free his father from a set of manacles. This Task is Difficulty 3, but Lorenz spends 2 Momentum to Create an Advantage to give him a set of lockpicks, which lowers the Difficulty of the Task to 2.

Combat Equipment

Weapons, armor, and other items used in combat have additional rules. Combat items are large, limiting how many you can carry and how easily they can be stowed away. They are usually carried in-hand, take up a significant amount of space in a bag or pack, or may be fitted with straps for easier carrying over the shoulder or on the back. All combat items are Major items. By default, a character’s inventory has 5 item slots, allowing them to carry five combat items at a time.

Some items are considered “bulky”, which means that they take up two inventory slots instead of one. Bulky items are big, difficult to transport, and cannot be concealed.

After character creation, most players may not need to adjust the combat items in their inventory. However, if players wish to do so, before combat begins, they may adjust the combat items in their inventory based on the circumstances of previous scenes or to switch out an item for a more or less useful one.

Weaponry

Weapons and other forms of attack, as well as the damage caused by them and by hazards, have a few characteristics that determine how they function. The key elements of a weapon are the weapon’s Type, Tag, Damage Rating, Size, and Qualities.

  • Type - Melee, Ranged, or Spell, showing how the weapon is used.
  • Tag - A weapon’s tag will determine which Attribute a character will use when making Tasks with that weapon.
  • Damage Rating - A number of [CD], as well as the Damage Effects that trigger when Effects are rolled.
  • All weapons gain additional [CD] to their damage rating equal to the Skirmish Skill of the character.
  • Size: Weapons are either one-handed (1H) or two-handed (2H). A 1H weapon only requires one hand to be used to wield it, allowing for the other to be left empty or carry another item. A 2H weapon requires both hands to wield. A 2H weapon can be used in one hand to make an attack, but the Difficulty increases by +1. A character wielding a one-handed weapon in two hands, or with a hand free, may re-roll 1d20 on the attack.
  • When dual wielding, one or both of the weapons being wielded must be 1H, and the character must choose which weapon they are attacking with before making the roll for the Task.
  • Qualities: Qualities are additional rules that provide additional restrictions or benefits to a weapon’s use.

Weapon Tags

In Ascension, all weapons will have one of the following weapon tags:

  • Swords refer generally to bladed weapons with short hilts. In the right hands, a Sword can make rapid strikes with dizzying maneuvers. Swords use Agility as their primary Attribute.
  • Axes refer generally to battleaxes, warhammers, and other heavy weapons. In the right hands, an Axe can swing great and powerful blows. Axes use Brawn as their primary Attribute.
  • Spears refer generally to polearms that can be thrusted or swung. In the right hands, a spear can strike precise and devastating blows from reach. Spears use Coordination as their primary Attribute.
  • Bows refer generally to ranged projectile weapons. In the right hands, a Bow can eliminate foes from a great distance, and are extra effective against flying opponents. Bows use Awareness as their primary Attribute.
  • Gauntlets refer generally to weapons that leave the hands open, such as bladed fists or armored gauntlets. In the right hands, Gauntlets can be used to rapidly disable opponents by tripping, grappling, and disarming them. Gauntlets can use Agility, Brawn, or Coordination as their primary Attribute.
  • Spells are not weapons, but in combat they serve a similar purpose. Attack spells can cause devastating and large effects at range, though the more powerful attack spells must be used sparingly to avoid draining the caster’s resources. Spell attacks use the character’s Magick Attribute (Presence, Faith, or Reason) as their primary Attribute.

Range

Melee weapons can only be used to attack enemies within Reach, unless they have the Ranged Quality.

  • Reach: Reach is the distance at which a character can use a melee weapon. By default, a weapon’s Reach is 1, so in order to target an object or character with a melee attack, they must be within 1 tile of (adjacent to) the wielder. If an ability or weapon quality (such as Extended) would extend a character’s Reach beyond 1, they can attack any target up to a distance equal to their Reach. A character’s Reach is equal to the Reach of the weapon they are currently wielding.
  • Range: All ranged weapons have an optimal Range, listed in the weapon’s stats. Range is measured starting from the attacking character, and a target must be within a weapon’s range in order to attempt an attack on them (e.g. a longbow’s range is 12, so attacks made with a longbow can target objects and creatures within 12 spaces of the attacker). If a character makes a Ranged Attack while within the target’s Reach, the difficulty of the task is increased by +1.

Damage Effects

The normal amount of damage caused by the weapon is expressed as a number of Challenge Dice ([CD]), before any increases for the character’s skills, actions taken, or Momentum spent. It may include damage effects as well, which trigger for Effects ([!]) rolled, copied below for reference.

Some damage effects are listed with an X, which is replaced by a number depending on the weapon and applies to every effect symbol that is rolled in the dice pool. If an effect would gain a rated damage effect that it already has, only the higher rated of the two applies.

  • Daunting X: The attack or hazard cuts into a target’s Willpower in addition to their HP. Add +X Willpower damage for each [!] rolled.
  • Destructive: The attack or hazard can quickly overcome physical obstacles, and deals double damage when targeting objects. When targeting an enemy unit, if the target is benefiting from Half-Cover and you roll 3 or more [!], you may reduce your damage by 2 in order to destroy that instance of Half Cover, and it can no longer be used for protection.
  • Draining: If a number of [!] are rolled that equals or exceeds the target’s Faith Effect Save, the target gains the Weakened condition until the end of their next turn.
  • Knockdown: The attack or hazard causes the target to stumble or fall. If a number of [!] are rolled that equals or exceeds the target’s Brawn Effect Save, the target is knocked prone.
  • Persistent [X]: The attack or hazard has a lingering effect. The target must succeed on a Difficulty 2 Brawn + Medicine Task at the end of their Turn or they suffer X [CD] damage (of the same type as the initial attack or hazard), and this continues for multiple rounds until they either succeed the check or until they benefit from a First Aid action. If a target accrues multiple instances of Persistent damage, the number of [CD] stacks. Persistent damage ignores resistance.
  • Pinning: If a number of [!] are rolled that equals or exceeds the target's Coordination Effect Save, they become immobilized and must spend a Minor Action to break free.
  • Provoking: If a number of [!] are rolled that equals or exceeds the target’s current Willpower, the target becomes Enraged until the end of their next turn, with the attacker as their source of rage.
  • Startling: If a number of [!] are rolled that equals or exceeds the target’s Awareness Effect Save, the target is Off-Guard until the end of their next turn.
  • Stunning: The attack or hazard leaves the target momentarily unable to act. If a number of [!] are rolled that equals or exceeds the target’s Awareness Effect Save, the target is Dazed until the end of their next turn.
  • Terrifying: If a number of [!] are rolled that equals or exceeds the target’s Willpower, the target is Frightened of you until they are consoled by an ally.

Effect Saves

Some damage effects give an enemy a Status if a number of effects are rolled equal to the Effect Save of an Attribute. Effect Saves are calculated by halving the Attribute (rounded down) and subtracting from the total. There are spaces on a character sheet to write these down so that they can be easily referenced.

Qualities

In addition to a weapon’s damage effects, a weapon may have any of the following Qualities, which affect how the weapon functions in combat.

  • Bulky: This weapon takes up two inventory slots instead of one.
  • Burst X: Attacks with this weapon affect characters within a radius of X, centered on and including the space occupied by the target. On a successful attack, characters within the radius but not the initial target are dealt half the attack’s initial damage and do not suffer any of the attack’s damage effects.
  • Close Quarters: This weapon is compact and easy to wield in tight confines and the press of melee. Attacks with this weapon suffer no penalty when used to make a ranged attack while within the target’s Reach.
  • Effortless: When this item is used in conjunction with another 1H weapon, you may reroll 1d20 when attacking with that weapon as if the hand holding this weapon was free.
  • Extended X: This weapon has Reach X. You may attack an adjacent target with this weapon even if they are 1 Height above or below you.
  • Heavy: Attacks with this weapon have +1 Difficulty unless the weapon is braced or you have a Brawn of 10 or higher. A 1H weapon is braced when it is wielded in two hands. A 2H weapon is braced if a Minor Action is spent to ready a stance before striking with it.
  • Knockback X: Successful attacks with this weapon push the target X spaces away in a direction of the attacker’s choice.
  • Loading: This weapon requires ammunition in order to be fired. You must spend a Minor Action to load this weapon before you may attack with it.
  • Parrying: When this weapon’s wielder makes an opposed test to defend against a melee attack, they may re-roll a single d20 on their test. This does not stack if the character has multiple Parrying weapons and cannot apply while wielding a weapon with the Spear tag.
  • Piercing: When resolving damage, ignore Resistance.
  • Reliable X: When you miss on an attack with this weapon, it still deals X damage. This damage applies after the counterstrike damage is dealt, if any.
  • Saddleback: This weapon is especially effective when used while mounted. When a character attacks with this weapon while mounted, they do not suffer the normal Increase in Difficulty from mounted attacks.
  • Subtle: Attacks with this weapon are difficult to detect. Attacks made while Hidden using a subtle weapon gain [CD] damage equal to the wielder’s Intrigue.
  • Thrown X: You can make up to X ranged attacks with this weapon before it is depleted. You may additionally use this weapon to make a melee attack that deals -2[CD], so long as it is not depleted.

Armor

In Ascension, there are four basic types of armor, in addition to shields, which provide varying degrees of coverage and protection, though sometimes with drawbacks.

All armor provides a certain number of Resistance, as well as certain qualities depending on what type of armor you are wearing. Armor takes up a slot of inventory, even when worn, and a character may only wear one suit of armor at a time. What your armor looks like is up to you, though you should take its type into account when determining that (e.g., light armor is good for characters trying to be stealthy, so likely wouldn’t be a full set of chainmail, and imposing armor is maximally protective, so likely isn’t going to be a simple padded gambeson).

Shields don’t provide Resistance, and instead provide certain buffs or abilities that help a character defend themselves in combat.

Resistance

Each form of armor provides an amount of Resistance. Resistance reduces damage inflicted by physical attacks, and is always expressed as a number.

Qualities

Some suits of armor may have one or more of the following Qualities:

  • Bulky: This armor takes up two inventory slots instead of one.
  • Concealing: Ranged attacks made against you gain +1 Difficulty. You provide Half-Cover to all adjacent allies.
  • Effortless: When this item is used in conjunction with a 1H weapon, you may reroll 1d20 when attacking with that weapon as if the hand holding this item was free.
  • Exhausting: This item is tiring to use. While this item is equipped, the wearer's speed and the speed of any mount they ride on is reduced by 2. This effect stacks if you have multiple Exhausting items equipped. Additionally, if you have this item equipped longer than a number of hours equal to your Brawn - 8 in a day, you suffer a Complication on every Task until you have sufficiently rested.
  • Overt X: This armor increases the Difficulty of any Task to Hide or be stealthy by X.
  • Parrying: When this item’s wielder makes an opposed test to defend against a melee attack, they may re-roll a single d20 on their test. This does not stack if the character has multiple Parrying items and cannot apply while wielding a weapon with the Spear tag.
  • Shield: While equipped, this item grants you a bonus die when defending against attacks.

General Equipment

Some items are not armor or weapons but still take up an inventory slot and grant certain bonuses to the wielder. They may still require a number of hands to wield and can have the bulky quality.

Item Name

Hands

Qualities

Description

Banner

1H

A banner shows your affiliation to a group, a house, or faction, and creates a sense of unity. While carrying one, you generate 1 Bonus Momentum for all Authority Combat Tasks.

Healing Potion

—

As a Minor Action, you can drink a Healing Potion and immediately restore HP equal to one health bar, and the Healing Potion is removed from your inventory. You may administer a potion to an adjacent ally as a Major Action.

Tome

—

Tomes are magic books or scrolls that increase the number of spells a spellcaster can use. As long as you already have spell slots, each tome you have in your inventory grants 2 additional spell slots.

Spell Implement

1H

A spell implement (e.g. an arcane orb, or a holy staff) is necessary to cast spells effectively. (See Chapter Eight: Magick)

Mounts

Players can augment their movement options by riding on a mount. All Tasks made while on a mount have a +1 Difficulty, and mounting or dismounting requires a Minor Action. While mounted, your Speed is effectively replaced by the mount’s. You may willingly roll off your mount with no action required, however this places you prone on the ground. If you are ever knocked prone, you automatically fall off your mount.

Mounts have different attributes associated to control them—called the Riding attribute. Most tasks related to controlling your mount use that attribute, which is described in the description of the specific mount.

If your HP is reduced to 0, you must make a Difficulty 3 Riding + Skirmish task, falling off your mount and landing Prone if you fail. Mounts have no health and cannot be targeted by attacks as long as they are being ridden. If you dismount from your mount, you may Dismiss it as a Minor Action, sending it away from the thick of battle to safety. You may recall your mount as a Major Action. If you do not Dismiss your mount after dismounting, it can be targeted by attacks (because mounts do not have stat blocks, attacks against them are Difficulty 1 and unopposed) and is Defeated if it takes any damage. When a mount is Defeated, it does not die, but is sent away from the battlefield and cannot be recalled until the end of the scene.

The Difficulty to make an attack with a bow against a target mounted on a flying creature decreases by 1, making flying units particularly vulnerable to archers.

Characters must have the Flier 1 talent in order to make use of flying mounts.

  • Horses - are a numerous and favored mount to take into battle. Riding is Coordination. A horse has a Speed equal to 6 + half your Riding (rounded down). Horses have difficulty when moving over difficult terrain—every space of movement over, onto, and off of difficult terrain costs thrice as much as standard.
  • Griffins are horse-like creatures with the head and wings of an eagle, allowing flight. Riding is Presence. A Griffin has a Speed equal to 5 + half your Riding (rounded down), and can fly.
  • Pegasi are majestic equine creatures with great feathery wings, said to have come from Heaven by some faiths. Riding is Faith. A Pegasus has a Speed equal to 5 + half your Riding (rounded down), and can fly.
  • Flying Brooms are magically enchanted broomsticks that are favored flying devices of wizards. Riding is Reason. A Flying Broom has a speed equal to 5 + half your Riding (rounded down), and flies. A broom cannot move on the ground, it must be flying to move.

Chapter Eight: Magick

In Ascension, characters can wield mighty spells in battle. There are three main domains of Magick: Arcane, Light, and Dark.

Arcane—also known as Wizardry, Sorcery, Alchemy, or sometimes simply Magick—is the Magick of manipulating the physical world. Arcane Magick can create, destroy, and transmute matter. The Arcane spellcaster can manipulate natural energy in the form of lightning, fire, and bitter cold. On the battlefield, a Wizard can devastate opponents with large areas of energy, teleport, and become invisible.

Light—also known as Miracle, Prayer, Channeling, or Incantation—is the Magick of the supernatural, granted to its wielder by forces greater than the physical world, most often attributed to the Divine. Light is the very essence of Life, and by channeling it a Light-wielder can instantaneously mend wounds. Light can be wielded in its raw form as a blinding energy, used to smite evildoers. Light can also be used to perform miracles that are impossible for a Wizard to accomplish by manipulating matter within the world, sensing souls and the like.

Dark—Also Known as Witchcraft, Blasphemy, and Shadow Magick-is the dark magick that exists at the fringes of what is known, and grants its user the tools to manipulate and strike at human souls directly. Dark Magick is seen as evil, or at least taboo, in nearly every culture, with its practitioners often staying at the fringes of society. On the battlefield, A Dark Mage can rend the very souls of their enemies, consume life force to empower themselves, and place blood curses.

Spellcasters

You are a Spellcaster if you have a Talent that grants spellcasting - these talents are Arcane Magick 1, Light Magick 1, and Dark Magick 1.

Magick Attribute

If you are a Spellcaster, you have a Magick Attribute that is determined by the Talent by which you have been granted spellcasting: Arcane Magick uses Reason; Light Magick uses Faith; and Dark Magick uses Presence. For example, if you have Light Magick and an ability of yours uses Magick + Medicine, you would Faith + Medicine, since Faith the Magick attribute for Light Magick.

If you have more than one Magick Domain (such as by having both Light Magick 1 and Arcane Magick 1), you have more than one Magick attribute. Any abilities granted solely by one of those domains must use the Magick Attribute associated with that domain - for example, a Spell prepared from the Arcane spell list using your Arcane spellcasting requires you to use Reason. However, abilities that do not have a prerequisite of a particular Domain - such as some Narrative talents - allow you to choose which Magick Attribute to apply.

Casting a Spell

Casting a Spell can take many forms. Taking an Action granted to you by a Spell, whether it be a Major Action, Minor Action, or Reaction, is considered Casting a Spell.

Each spell will have a Tier and a number of Uses listed in its description. Taking the first tier of any spellcasting Talent (e.g. Arcane Magick 1 or Light Magick 1) grants you the ability to prepare Tier 1 spells from your respective domain. Higher tier spells can be unlocked by taking higher level Talents. In addition to its tier, each spell’s uses determine how many times you can use a spell during a scene. Higher level Magick Domain Talents unlock more uses for your spells.

A Passive spell is not Cast—rather, its effects are continuous as long as the spell is prepared.

Spell Slots

A Spellcaster has Spell Slots equal to their Study. If you have Spell Slots, you may prepare Spells that take up a total of Spell Slots that you have (some spells take up more than 1 Spell Slot). If you have access to a Magick Domain, you can prepare any of the spells from that Magick Domain's Spell list that you meet the prerequisites for. You may prepare multiple copies of the same spell to be able to use it more often in a scene.

You can increase your number of Spell Slots by equipping a Tome (see Equipment).

Between Scenes, you may replace any spells you have prepared for any other that you meet the prerequisites for.

Spell Implement

To cast spells effectively, the spellcaster must hold a Spell Implement in one of their hands. Without a Spell Implement, the Difficulty of all Tasks involved in the casting of spells increases by 1. This affects Tasks such as Attack with attack spells, but not Tasks that a spell enhances or alters — for example, not having a Spell Implement does not increase the Difficulty of making an Attack that was enhanced using a Spellblade spell.

If a Character is only holding a Spell Implement and nothing else in their other hand, or both hands on one Spell Implement, they generate 1 Bonus Momentum for Spellcasting Tasks.

Spell Tags

Spells have a variety of tags that label what sort of Magick it is. These tags do not have any inherent rules associated with them, but many Talents and other abilities refer to them.

Casting a Spell

If a Spell can be Cast, the Action required to cast it is described in its description. Most spells require a Major Action to cast, but many use Minor Actions, Reactions, and Free Actions.

A Passive spell is not Cast - rather, its effects are continuous as long as the spell is prepared.

Spell Attacks

Many spells involve making a Spell Attack when they are used. A Spell Attack counts as an Attack, similar to an Attack with a weapon. Unless stated otherwise, making an Attack with an Attack spell follows the same rules as making any other attack, and is a task of Magick + Skirmish—the attribute it is Defended is stated in the Spell’s description. A Spell Attack can also be a Ranged Attack or a Melee Attack, determined by the Spell’s description - though some Spell Attacks might be considered neither.

If a Spell Attack deals damage, add your Skirmish to the number of [CD] listed in the spell’s description (as you would when determining a Weapon’s damage).

Range and Reach

Ranged Spells have a listed Range. If a Spell has a listed Reach instead, then it is considered a Melee Spell.

Areas of Effect

Some spells have special Qualities that give them unique Areas of Effect. When multiple characters would be affected by an Area of Effect spell attack, each character in the area attempts a defense roll, but only one attack roll is made.

  • Blast X is a circular area that originates from a Space and affects spaces within a radius of X spaces. For example, a spell with a range of 10 and Blast 3 can originate from a space up to 10 Spaces from the caster, then affects all Spaces that extend up to 3 Spaces away.
  • Line X affects units in all Spaces in a line that is X spaces long. A Line can have a width for multiple Spaces, but if no width is specified then it has a width of a Single space.
  • Cone X affects units within a cone shaped area that is X spaces long and X spaces wide at its widest point. All cones are 1 space wide at their narrowest point.

Part Five: Armies and Mass Combat

Chapter Nine: Armies

When hostilities between political powers reach a boiling point and war goes from inevitable to immediate, there comes a point where armies must be raised. While many battles in Ascension focus on smaller scale combat involving only the party and some group of individual assailants, there may come a point where instead of acting just as individual combatants, player characters instead take on the role of military officers of an entire army.

A party in Ascension will most often have a single army that they lead, train, and expand over the course of a campaign. Armies are made up of many individual people, whose number, training, and abilities are represented by the different facets of an army: Divisions, Scale, Talents, and its Traits. Though some of these facets, like an army’s Scale or Divisions, may change over time, what players invest in their army, like Talents and its Defining Feature, will remain consistent.

Divisions

Armies are composed of a number of divisions that have different specializations on the battlefield. These can include footsoldiers, cavalry, griffin riders, medical units, to name a few. Each army can have up to a number of divisions equal to its scale. Each division that an army has also counts as a Trait for that army.

Each Division will have its own resistance, features, and a buff that it grants to nearby officers. Divisions also have Types that denote what kind of division it is. Certain types of division will be stronger or weaker to other types, and this should be considered when recruiting divisions for your army.

Each division has a base attack that can only be made against other divisions labeled with a damage rating and if the attack is ranged.

Scale

An army’s scale represents the number of soldiers marching with the army. As a general rule, for every point of scale, the army doubles in size. An army may have a number of divisions equal to its scale. Additionally, if an army brings fewer divisions to battle than its scale allows, all divisions start the battle with 1 extra point of morale and roll 1 extra [CD] on attacks against other divisions for every point of scale above the number brought.

Most armies that enter battle tend to be between scale 3 and 6, but battles can involve armies much bigger or smaller than that. In a small-scale conflict between two towns, they might only have scale 1-2 armies. In a massive war between empires in a well populated region, they might use scale 7-10. Above that, it is usually better to represent the scale of an empire’s force by giving them multiple high scale armies, instead of one massive army.

Scale

Army Size

1

A band of thieves

2

A town militia

3

A mercenary army

4

The army of a county or minor noble

5

A raised army of an independent city

6

The army of a wealthy independent duchy

7

The army of a mid-sized kingdom

8

The army of a large and wealthy kingdom

9

A rising empire’s army

10

A massive empire’s army

Talents

Army Talents are specific abilities or advantages that your army provides during narrative play, based on your army’s areas of expertise or special training. Army Talents provide similar benefits as a character’s Narrative Talents, only they originate from the presence of your army rather than from your character’s actions and behaviors.

Traits

Each army has Traits, which work the same way Traits do for player characters: they are neutral facts about the army that may be used to reduce the Momentum or Threat costs to Create Advantages or Complications as relevant. An army will gain most of its Traits from the Divisions that it has currently recruited, and it will also have a Defining Feature Trait that is determined by the players as they create their army.

Building an Army

Armies come in many shapes and sizes, so when building the party’s primary army it is worthy considering the needs and focus of the army when it operates.

Step One: Determine an Army’s Scale. The GM sets the scale of the players’ army depending on the narrative circumstances of the army: Who is funding this army? What is this army going to be used for? Where is this army located? The scale of an army may change over time depending on the answers to these questions, and the army may need to be adjusted accordingly when these changes take place.

Step Two: Recruit Divisions. An army can recruit a number of divisions each to its scale. Every division type has its own benefits and drawbacks that should be considered when selecting them, and the availability of the divisions that players may choose from will be set by the GM. Certain divisions may not be easily recruitable and may require narrative effort before they can be added to your army.

Step Three: Choose Talents. Your army gains a number of Talents depending on the level of the player characters in charge of it:

  • Level 0-3: Your army gains 1 Talent.
  • Level 4-7: Your army gains 2 Talents.
  • Level 8-11: Your army gains 3 Talents.
  • Level 12: Your army gains 4 Talents.

 For a list of Army Talents, see Chapter Eleven: Building Blocks of an Army.

Step Four: Set Traits. Your army gains a Trait for each unique Division that it has (e.g. if an army has two Mages divisions, it will only have one Mages Trait). It also gains a Defining Feature: a unique Trait decided upon by all players. This Trait will likely relate to the army’s purpose or its highest authority. For example, a mercenary army might have “Mercenary Army” as its Defining Feature, while an army that is the standing force for a kingdom might have “The King’s Army” as its Defining Feature.

Example Army Creation

After negotiating the support of Duchess Marcella, Adelinde and her companions have secured the funding to raise their own army to stand against the king. In order to build their army, the GM must first determine the army’s scale. Duchess Marcella is wealthy, but she has her own forces to maintain and isn’t investing all her resources into the party’s cause. As a result, the party’s army should be fairly small to begin with, so the GM decides to set the scale of their army at 3.

Because their army has scale 3, the party is able to recruit up to three divisions. Duchess Marcella is Thaloran and has a great amount of influence on the local wizardry academy, and she offers to give the party connections to some mages looking for work if they’re interested. As a result, the party is able to hire up to two Mage Divisions. However, Adelinde wants at least one infantry division to cancel out the advantage that any enemy infantry might give their opponents, and Rylan wants a Bowman division to give them a bonus to their bow attacks, so they decide to only recruit one division of Mages. For their infantry, Adelinde picks a Light Footmen division so that she can use their feature to give Orders to that Division as a minor action.

The party is currently at Level 4, so they get to choose 2 Talents for their army. Anticipating that they will need to use their army to seize several strongholds of the king, the party picks Siege Masters as one of their Talents. For their second Talent, Erik suggests Mess Tents. 

Finally, the party must set their army’s Traits. Currently, their three divisions are Mages, Bowmen, and Light Footmen, so those are the army’s first three Traits. For the army’s Defining Feature, the party discusses amongst themselves for a while about what to do. Because their army’s ultimate goal is fighting against their tyrannical king and hoping to gather more strength to depose him, the party gives their army the Defining Feature: “Rebels against the King.”

Leveling up your Army

Most aspects of your army are determined by the needs of the story rather than the army or the player’s level. However, the longer you spend with your army, the more training it can receive. When players reach levels 4, 8, and 12, their army gains one additional Army Talent.

Chapter Ten: Mass Combat

In Ascension, mass combat refers to any battle in which an army or armies are involved. Like smaller scale combat, mass combat utilizes a battlefield, with every officer in the involved armies occupying a single space as they would in standard combat. Individual soldiers, however, are not depicted on the field, instead each assumed to be part of various divisions of the armies they serve in. It is assumed that all characters on the battlefield hold some degree of rank or command over their side's army, with the exception of narrative NPCs who might serve as targets for protection, capture, or assassination.

The army itself is represented more abstractly. Instead of occupying individual spaces as officers do, each army is split into multiple divisions which each are located within a designated region on the battlefield called a zone. Zones are made up of some number of contiguous spaces on the map that often share a specific characteristic, such as being atop the same hill, along the bank of a riverbed, or the inside of a fortress’s walls. When officers move to spaces within the same zone as one or more allied divisions, they gain buffs from fighting alongside their soldiers and can issue the army orders to engage in more direct skirmishes with the enemy.

However even with the presence of an army, the core of combat remains the same: units on the field skirmishing against enemy units. Even with some potentially new responsibilities to track, players should remember that an army is only as strong as its last standing officer and will usually spend the majority of their effort battling and defeating enemy officers. But by utilizing the army effictively—relocating troops to advantageous positions, driving back dangerous enemy divisions, and using cunning stratagems to dominate the battlefield—victory can be assured.

The Basics of Battle

During the battle, player characters move across the battlemap engaging with enemy officers placed onto the field as they would in small-scale combat. As they do, divisions are denoted on the battlefield alongside them, but instead of occupying specific spaces on the map, they exist broadly within different zones on the battlefield (see Battlefield Zones).

Orders

The most core element to making two armies clash on the battlefield is issuing orders. These allow divisions to undertake certain actions to affect the battlefield. Most orders require the use of a Major Action, and unless otherwise stated, officers may only issue orders to divisions within the same zone.

Each division may only be issued one Order per round.

List of Army Orders

The basic orders available to officers are:

  1. Army Attack: The officer orders a division to make an attack. See Making Army Attack, below, for a full explanation.
  2. Reposition: The officer performs a Difficulty 1 Presence + Authority task. On a success, they may order any number of divisions in the same zone to move to any adjacent zone, or any number of divisions in an adjacent zone to move into the current zone. On a failure, they may only order one division to move.

This order may be used to allow a division to move even if it has already taken a Free Move, or to move across a Hazardous zone border, provoking a Mass Opportunity Attack if applicable (see below).

  1. Regroup: The Officer orders a division to tend its wounded and return to battle. The officer performs a Difficulty 1 Faith + Authority task, or Difficulty 2 if the division is broken. On a success, the division regains 2 + the officer’s authority [CD]. If the division was broken, it no longer is.
  1. Broken divisions may be ordered to Regroup, even if they have already been issued an order this round.
  1. Stratagem: The Officer orders a division to perform a special ability granted by its stratagem. See Stratagems.

Free Moves

Additionally, once per turn, an officer may, as a free action, order a division to make a Free Move across any accessible zone border (see moving between zones). The officer may either order a division in their current zone to move out, or a division in an adjacent zone to move in.

Once a division has moved this way, it may not move again this way until the next round. At the end of a round, any divisions that have not taken a Free Move may do so, even if an officer is not present.

Reactions

Brace

When a division is the target of an attack, an officer in the same zone may use a reaction to have the division brace against the attacking force. When this occurs, the task becomes opposed, allowing the defending officer to roll using their Presence + Authority.

Mass Opportunity Attack

When enemy divisions enter or leave the same zone as an officer across a Hazardous border, the officer may order all allied divisions in the zone to make a Mass Opportunity Attack. The officer performs an attack skill test, allowing an enemy officer on either side of the crossed border to Brace. On a success, each of the officer’s allied divisions may deal damage to a single enemy division that crossed the border. On a failure, the enemy divisions are unharmed, but may not counterstrike.

A division may only participate in one Mass Opportunity Attack each round.

Attacks and Damage

Making Army Attacks

When issue an attack order, follow these steps:

  • Attacker selects the attacking division: The ordering officer selects the division to order to attack, usually a division in the same zone.
  • Attacker chooses target: The attacker chooses the target for the attack. This will usually be an opposing division in the same zone.
  • Skill Test: The officer performs a Difficulty 1 Presence + Authority Task.
  • If the defending division is braced, the task is instead performed as an Opposed Task against the bracing officer’s Presence + Authority.
  • Outcome: If the attacker officer succeeds or wins the contest, then the division inflicts damage on the target, as described below in Army Damage. If the defending officer wins the contest, the defending division may counterstrike, if able. Like with attacks between characters, ranged attacks may not be counterstruck even when defended against.

Army Damage

When rolling damage for a division, roll a number of [CD] equal to its damage rating plus the authority of the ordering officer.

Unlike individual characters, an army’s health is considered through the morale of its divisions. A division’s morale starts with a morale of 8, plus any bonus from the army’s scale, and can be reduced when the division is attacked or nearby officers are defeated.

When a division is damaged, its morale is reduced equal to the damage taken, subtracting the division’s resistance if relevant. If a division takes damage and there is no allied officer in the same zone, the attacker may also force it to retreat.

Officer Defeats

When a basic officer is defeated in battle, all allied divisions in the same zone take 1 morale damage, ignoring any resistance. When a player character or an NPC with multiple health bars is defeated, allied divisions in the same zone take damage equal to their number of health bars (i.e. three for a player, two or three depending on the NPC). Defeated chaff do not deal morale damage to divisions.

Defeating Divisions

If a division’s morale is reduced to zero, it becomes Broken and may be forced to retreat by the attacker (see below). A Broken division no longer provides its support buff to any officers or any passive effects and cannot move or be issued orders other than Regroup. A division remains Broken unless targeted by the Regroup order.

Retreating Divisions

When a division is attacked, it may be forced to retreat. Most often this occurs when the division is broken. When given the option to have a target division retreat, the attacker chooses an adjacent zone for the division to forcibly relocate to. A division may not retreat to a zone that has an enemy division or across a zone border that is impassable.

The Battlefield

Mass combat battlefields are no different from the environments for standard battles. They may be great open fields, a series rolling hills, the flats outside of castle walls, the streets of a sprawling city, or other such arenas. The Gamemaster may give the terrain different traits that impact the navigability of the environment by making it easier or more difficult to move around, gain cover, interact with objects, etc. Hazards and complications created with threat by the game master during battle can also affect tasks performed by the armies during battle.

Battlefield Zones

Instead of being represented directly on the battlefield, army divisions are more abstracted. While the army’s officers are placed on the battlefield as normal, utilizing grid spaces to move across the terrain as they would in standard combat, armies instead occupy battlefield zones.

A battlefield zone is a subdivision of spaces or a region on the battlefield that can support an army. A battlefield can have any number of zones—a minor battle between two small armies may only have three, while the site of the clash between massive forces could have seven or eight. As a general rule, a battlefield should always have a maximum number of zones equal to the divisions in the largest of the engaging armies.

Zones should aim to be of roughly similar size, and should take up anything equal to between a 5x5 area to a 12x12 area, depending on the size of the battlefield.

Moving Between Zones

Officers are not affected by zones when moving and will move freely between zones as they move across the battlefield. Divisions must move from zone to zone as they progress across the battlefield, crossing over zone borders as they do.

Borders between zones can be either considered Accessible, Hazardous, or Impassable. A border is considered Accessible if there is no impediment to moving across it, such as over an open field. A zone border is considered hazardous if crossing it requires moving through or into difficult terrain, such as over a trench, uphill, or into a forest (see Terrain below). A border is impassable if it is composed entirely of impassable terrain.

Every round, each division is allowed one Free Move to an adjacent zone so long as the border is Accessible. Once per turn, an officer may, as a free action, order a division in the same zone to Free Move out of the current zone, or a division in an adjacent zone to Free Move into the current zone. If a division’s Free Move has not been used by the end of a round, it may move across an Accessible border into any adjacent zone to its current position, regardless of whether an allied officer is present.

In order to cross a Hazardous zone border, a division must be issued a reposition order. When divisions cross a hazardous border, they may provoke a Mass Opportunity Attack if there is an enemy division and officer present in the zone being moved into.

Divisions may not cross an Impassable border unless they have the Flying type. Additionally, any border composed entirely of Perilous Water is considered Impassable for divisions.

Terrain

The placement of terrain can affect the movement of army divisions. Terrain can often define the borders of zones—such as slopes, walls, rivers, trenches, etc. Armies need at least two spaces of normal terrain along a border to use a Free Move. If the entire border between two zones is difficult terrain or the zone is considered difficult terrain, the border is considered Hazardous and requires a reposition order to move across.

If the majority of tiles within a zone are of a specific type of terrain, that zone is also considered that terrain. If a zone is considered difficult terrain, all of its borders are Hazardous. Some terrain types have additional effects for armies:

  • If a zone is majority forest tiles, all divisions within it gain Half Cover.
  • If a zone is majority Deep Water, all tasks for attack and defending orders have a Difficulty increase of 2.
  • Divisions may not enter a zone that is majority Perilous Water for any reason.

Structures

Buildings, infrastructure, and objects on the battlefield that take up spaces can be considered Structures. Structures are parts of the battlefield that are subject to damage or demolition on account of the actions of armies. To account for this, structures are considered to have some amount of health that, when reduced to zero, leads to a part of all of the structure to be damaged or destroyed.

Some structures may be too massive to be able to be wholly destroyed in one go, like a city’s walls or a massive bridge. For these structures, you may want to divide them into segments on the map that can be targeted by attacks, such that one part of the structure can be destroyed without bringing the entire thing down. For example, if a combat encounter involves sieging a walled city, you might have 3 segments of wall on the map, each with their own HP. When one segment of wall is destroyed, it allows an opening into the city where that segment was, but the remaining walls are unaffected until they are also attacked and dealt damage.
