Part Seven: Lore

Chapter Fifteen: The World of Edhela

Welcome to Edhela, a medieval world rife with political and religious and magical struggle, where peasants toil to enrich their noble lords while the princes of both Church and State wage their wars on the backs of levied soldiers and mercenaries alike. This is a world of inequality, of tyranny, and of the Divine Right of Kings. But nevertheless, this is also a world full of people: people who dream of better lives, who taste hope on the wind, people striving to make something better from the circumstances they were given.

The setting of Edhela is meant to be one where fantasy and historical realism exist side by side, or as side by side as they can. In the world of Edhela, it’s taken for granted that monarchs and nobility not only have the right to rule, but the only right. Religion and gender and the oppression of the monarchy are aspects of this setting that are meant to provide both the feeling of the past and to provide a basis for the conflicts and tensions that make a story interesting. Discomfort with certain elements of this setting is more than possible and at times to be expected: our own medieval past is not clean or easy, neither is this setting.

But once this book is in your hands, this world is yours to play in. Please change what needs to be changed, add what you think is fun to add, and mold Edhela to your liking as you tell your own stories here.

The Edhelan Empire

The Edhelan Empire, known to some as the Holy Edhelan Empire, is the current highest form of sovereign authority on the continent of Edhela, containing and ruling over all of the nations of Paerdland, Thalore, Oriande, and the Meian Isles. It is ruled by an emperor, originally chosen by electors from each nation, who passes their crown down to a chosen successor who cannot be related to the emperor by blood. Currently, the empire is ruled by Rosalinde Hypaerion, its first emperor, who has yet to choose her successor.

  • Rosalinde Hypaerion. Chosen during the negotiations that created the Edhelan Empire, Rosalinde is Edhela’s first emperor, elected for her strength of will, leadership, and the brave deeds she committed during the course of the Great War. Though it was not asked of her, she ceded her title as the duke of Northmont to her son, Averil Hypaerion, upon ascending the imperial throne in order to remain devoted solely to the interests of all of Edhela. Averil was a child at the time, so her husband ruled in his stead until he came of age, and as a result, Emperor Rosalinde has spent much of her reign ruling alone in Dorhem, while her family has stayed in Northmont.

The capital of the empire is the city of Dorhem, an old and sacred city to the Arysian faith, which also calls Dorhem its capital. Though Dorhem was once considered part of Paerdland, it was declared a neutral territory as part of the Edict of Edhela, and is now ruled solely by the emperor. Before the empire, the Church ruled Dorhem directly, albeit still as a landed vassal of Paerdland. Though this decision was made freely by the pontifex at the time, Pontifex Aoric III, it has since become the subject of some tension between the Church and the Imperial Court, as later pontiffs (including the current Pontifex Margery) have butted heads with the emperor over issues like taxation and who has jurisdiction over crimes that occur in Dorhem and the surrounding lands.

While the role of the empire in Edhela may sometimes be contested by its vassals (such as the War of the Marquises in Thalore, spurred when Thaloran nobles rebelled against the empire’s taxation policies), its primary function is to be a unifier, peace-bringer, and negotiator for Edhela’s disparate nations. To that effect, the empire has instituted several policies since its inception, aimed at bringing greater unity to the continent:

  • The Imperial Army: Motivated by the harrowing losses and the severe destruction wrought on both sides of the Great War, one of the first policies enacted during the creation of the empire was the creation of an Imperial Army. While each nation is allowed to maintain its own standing armies to protect themselves and their lands, the empire’s standing army is substantially bigger and stronger than each individual nation’s army, with its men-at-arms raised and maintained by the significant levies imposed on each nation. The Imperial Army is a formidable force, a testament to the strength of Edhela’s newfound unity, as well as a deadly warning to any who might entertain thoughts of conflict against their neighbors or against the empire itself.
  • In order for the emperor to use the imperial armies, each nation must cast a vote on whether they approve or not. If the majority of nations agree, the emperor can then muster their forces, but cannot if the majority disagree. In the event of a tie, the pontifex casts the tie breaking vote.
  • The Imperial Coinage: After the creation of the empire came the creation of a new universal currency: the imperial crown, a gold coin meant to be used across Edhela with no need for exchange. While many places still utilize and produce a local currency, imperial crowns have become very popular amongst merchants and traders, and most regional coins in Edhela are minted with the intent to bear an equivalent value.
  • The Imperial Calendar: Before the establishment of the empire, the standard in Edhela was, for the most part, to use the Arysian Calendar, which divided history into two eras: Before Arys (B.A.) and Anno Vatis (Year of the Prophet; A.V.). Now that the Great War is concluded, and to aid in ushering in a new era of peace and unity, the Empire has issued a new imperial calendar, whose first year begins in the year that the empire was founded.

[Sidebar] Making Edhela’s Characters Your Own

When it comes to characters established by the lore described in this book, they are meant as tools for you to use to craft your story, not as dogma. If you would rather create your own character to be the Edhelan Emperor, or if you want to change the name of one of the noble houses listed, that is left up to the discretion of the GM.

Places in the Empire

There are four major nations that make up the continent of Edhela: Paerdland, Thalore, the Meian Isles, and the Republic of Oriande.

Paerdland

The Kingdom of Paerdland is a small, northern kingdom with a visual aesthetic similar to England in the 1300s. It is a cold and forested land, broken up into duchies and counties held by the king’s noble vassals. The kingdom itself is ruled by the Royal House of Glaziere, which has ruled Paerdland in an unbroken line for hundreds of years, currently headed by King Ceolmunde and his queen-consort, Valora of Lejren. Paerdland has a long cultural tradition of gender equality and equal succession, due in part because it is the birthplace of the Arysian faith, which holds gender equality as a core tenet. As the birthplace of the faith and the current location of the seat of the Church, Paerdland is a fiercely devout nation, and the influence of the Church is strongest here.

  • Druids. In the mountains that mark Paerdland’s eastern border dwell nomadic clans of druids: people who still observe the Old Ways that once dominated Paerdland before the advent of the Arysian Church. The druids keep away from the cities and towns of Paerdland, both to stay more closely connected to nature in its wildest forms, but also to avoid the ire of the Church, which wholly condemns those still practicing pagan faiths.
  • Capital: Keldholme
  • Duchies: Keldholme and its Crownlands, held by Royal House Glaziere; Northmont, held by House Hypaerion; Bjarün, held by House Wainwright; Narrow Coast, held by House Rothlain; Orgaard, held by House Varnhame; Lamgenborough, held by House Bradian; Gengham, held by House Harcourt; and Ravensworth, held by House Complyn.

Thalore

The Queendom of Thalore is a large, southern polity with a visual aesthetic similar to 1300s Spain. It is currently held by the Royal House of Aendryndel, headed by Queen Adthana ter Aendryndel. It is warmer in climate than Paerdland, with a heavily forested western peninsula and scrubland to the east, dotted with the tall, spire towers favored by Thaloran nobility. Thalore is the birthplace of arcane magic, and its culture and society is dominated by the veneration of magic; nearly all of Thalore’s upper classes (noble and merchant) are made up of wizards. Thalore has a matriarchal culture dominated by the idea that women are naturally predisposed to be better at magic while men are weaker, duller creatures who cannot and should not wield the arcane, often relegated to the “masculine” duties of keeping a home and childrearing, as well as the lowly status of doing martial, non-magical warfare. Thaloran matriarchy is further perpetuated in Thalore’s female only succession law that also prevents inheritance through the male line. While the influence of the Church is strong in Thalore, there have often been conflicts between Thalore and the Church, particularly over matters of inheritance and magical law where the Thaloran crown asserts its right to its own inheritance laws and its own laws governing the use of magic, above that of the Church.

  • Arcane Academies. Much like how great cathedrals and monasteries of medieval Europe often commanded the same power and wealth as secular baronies, Thalore is dotted by feudal desmenses that belong to its arcane academies. These institutions are places of arcane learning, where members of the aristocracy are taught to do magic and continuously research and enhance the magical knowledge that fuels Thalore’s might. The arcane academies owe their own fealty and pay taxes to the ducal overlords whose territories they reside in, and the most prestigious of these is the Royal Arcane Academy, vassal to the royal house of Aendryndel and located in its capital city.
  • Capital: Badura
  • Duchies: Badura and its Crownlands, held by Royal House Aendryndel; Hightower, held by House Rothenel; Ilacante, held by House Trevarieth; Trevanwood, held by House Nevarro; the Iron Mountains, held by House Galakir; Falcois, held by House Holaren; the Nevyrr Bluffs, held by House Carvaris; and Emirselia, held by House Laemirsel.

The Meian Isles

The Meian Isles are a loose collaboration of many different islands to Edhela’s far north, each ruled by its own jarl. There is a Council of Jarls made up of each island’s jarl, though it is less a true overarching governing body and more of a war council, handling matters of military conflict and relations with the mainland. The head of the council is the prince of Fnjoska, currently Prince Eydís of Fnjoska. The other isles are Breivik, Herdla, Setsaa, Lejren, Kvanne, Torskulla, and Kjerland. Idsal, a territory on the northern coast of Paerdland, is also ruled by the Isles, with its own Jarl on the council.

Much like Paerdland, the Meian Isles has a cultural tradition of gender equality and equal succession, though the influence of the Church is much less so than on the continent, due to the Isles’ distance and isolation, especially further north. The Meian Isles have a very strong navy, and are a fierce, seafaring people who, in addition to their involvement in wars on the mainland, are often embroiled in conflict with the giants who live in the far north and make incursions south. Thus, most adult Meians have some experience either as soldiers or as sailors on Meian longboats (often both), as the Isles are rarely ever not fighting against some threat to the north or south.

  • The Giants. Not much is known about the Giants who dwell in the far north, save that they are massive, humanoid creatures of incredible size and strength, and that they seek ever to drive humans out of their lands and strongholds. The forces of the Meian Isles are Edhela’s first line of defense against the giants to the north, often accompanied by Paerdish strength, and it is these noble soldiers who protect Edhela from widespread giant incursions.
  • Capital: Nowhere officially, but Fnjoska hosts meetings of the Council of Jarls.
  • Isles: Breivik; Herdla; Setsaa; Lejren; Kvanne; Torskulla; Kjerland; and Idsal (actually a part of the mainland).

Oriande

The Republic of Oriande governs the massive swatch of land west of the Skiljar mountains that divide Edhela’s continent in two. The wide expanse of fields and hills are home to large amounts of farmland and many rural, somewhat isolated villages. The republic arose after the fall of the Orvhallen Empire, the millenia spanning empire that once covered nearly all of the continent before it was brought low in the Irym War. Unlike the eastern kingdoms, Oriande has no nobility, and its people are divided into two classes: the aristocratic patricians and the more common plebeians, though all are commoners in the eyes of eastern nobility. The republic is ruled by the Senate, a legislative body made up of 45 patrician senators and led by its two consuls, which is seated in the far western city of Vatera. The consuls are elected by the people of Vatera, and the senators are in turn appointed by the elected consuls. The republic is known throughout Oriande and beyond for its corruption and ineffectiveness outside of Vatera and the surrounding Orvhala region, giving the other major cities of Oriande extreme latitude and even relative independence, though all recognize the supremacy of the senate at least in name. Oriande is dominated by a patriarchal culture, in which women are often viewed as inferior, and many patrician families practice male preferred succession. However, while it is often quite difficult for women to achieve power and independence in Oriande, it is not impossible, and there are several women serving in the Senate, as well as one of the consuls, Hristina Stamideos.

  • Mercenaries. Unlike the eastern kingdoms of Paerdland and Thalore, which primarily rely on levies, most cities and local powers in Oriande lack standing armies of any kind or a conscription system, instead relying on professional soldiers for hire for defense and military conflicts. The only standing army in Oriande is the Republican Army of the Commonwealth, a small standing army maintained in Vatera that acts as the official military of Oriande. The Republican Army’s primary role is to defend the capital, though it has been used in the past for greater military conflict such as during the Reformation Wars or The Great War. In times of war, it is often augmented with mercenary forces.
  • Capital: Vatera
  • Major Former City-States: Vatera; Develtos; Arketsa; Izmir; Lanuvum; Pisae; and Adana.

Outer Realms

Beyond the main continent of Edhela are the outer realms, where people and nations exist that are far from Edhela and often have wildly different worldviews and cultures from what exists there. The major powers that are known to exist beyond the borders of Edhela are Meravía, and Hraezla.

Meravía is an archipelago nation to the far southeast of Edhela that serves as a major hub of trade between Edhela and the lands to the far south and east. Thanks to its importance as a tradeport, Meravía has become incredibly wealthy with a vast navy, and it has many ties to Thalore and Oriande as the coastal Edhelan nations closest to it. Meravía has its own version of the Arysian Church, created when the Southern Church broke off from the mainland church over theological differences. Meravía is ruled by a council comprised of the nation’s guild leaders and the Pontifex of the Southern Church called “The Council of Luminaries.”

Hraezla is a kingdom to the far north of the Meian Isles, west of Giant Country, where it is extremely cold and mountainous. While technically on the same continent as Edhela, Hraezla is not a part of the Empire and for the most part keeps to itself, easily done thanks to the Dragonspine mountains that separate it from its southern neighbors. These mountains are also home to dragons, larged, winged, fire-breathing beasts. Hraezlans have learned to live amidst the threat of dragonfire, and have even domesticated smaller wyverns for their use as mounts. Beyond this, not a lot is known about Hraezla outside of the Meian Isles, where wyvern riders are sometimes known to go raiding for livestock and food stores.

Religion in Edhela

Religion is one of the most important aspects of all life in Edhela, as people of all kinds orient their lives and their beliefs around their faith. The dominant religion in Edhela is the Arysian Faith, a monotheistic  hierarchical institution much like the Catholic Church of the medieval period. Because of its cultural and political influence, the Church is often oppressive towards those who do not follow its teachings, particularly towards those it deems heretics.

The Arysian Faith

The Arysian faith is the dominant monotheistic religion in the northern lands of the Known World, with most of Edhela and Merevía’s populations being adherents of the faith, called Arysians. The Arysian faith began in the 16th century Priori Imperium (or the first century Anno Vatis, in the original Arysian calendar) with the life and teachings of a woman named Arys, who is said to have walked and spoken with Onyame Themself, the Sovereign and Creator of everything.

Origins of the Faith. The Arysian faith began in the first century A.V. (Anno Vatis) with the life and teachings of a woman named Arys, who is said to have walked and spoken with Onyame, the Divine Being and Almighty God. Arys received the revelation of Onyame’s existence and Their Divine Instruction for humanity when she was but a poor shepherd in the mountains of Paerdland, and afterwards traveled Paerdland preaching the Word of Onyame and accruing followers. Arys was known for performing awe-inspiring miracles during her time as a minister, including summoning great pillars of light and flame, healing the sick and lame, and casting out dark spirits from the possessed.

Arys’ message was one of hope and goodness, that everyone was born imbued with the Light of Onyame and thus gifted with the power to do good and to love, and that if they chose to heed the Light within them, to do good unto others and to love others as they did themselves, then they could gain eternal life in Heaven. At the end of her years of travel and teaching, Arys instructed her followers to continue her work and spread the Word of God across Edhela, then she left for the mountains to hear the word of Onyame again and never returned. It is the belief of her followers that Onyame brought Arys up to the Heavens to join Them. The remains of Arys’ followers recorded her teachings and about 300 years later, the accounts were compiled into a single holy book: The Holy Chronicle of St. Arys.

For about 200 years after Arys was taken into the heavens, the faith was a mostly unorganized cult of followers wandering Paerdland and Thalore, spreading Arys’ teachings. This cult was centered in Dorhem--the city where St. Arys spent much of her time. It was only upon the end of the Reclamation War that the Arysian faith actually organized into a formal, hierarchical Church.

Tenets of Faith. The basic ideas/beliefs of the Arysian faith are based on the following tenets:

  • There is no god other than Onyame, who is the one and only God, and Creator of Heaven and Earth. Onyame is all powerful, and the source of all that is Good and True.
  • St. Arys was and is the instrument of Onyame on earth, the rod through which Onyame’s Divine Presence was revealed to Their people. St. Arys was chosen by Onyame, she saw Their radiant face, and her words are the Word of Onyame. St. Arys did not die, but was assumed into Heaven and sits at the right hand of Onyame.
  • The Word of Onyame and the revelations of St. Arys are revealed in the Holy Chronicle which is a divinely inspired and sacred text.
  • Esum, Chaos, is real, and is the source of all discord and chaos in the world.
  • The Church is the vehicle through which Onyame acts on earth. It’s structure and authority are given by Onyame, and its leadership was conferred and ordained by St. Arys herself.

Tenets of Worship. The Arysian faith is widespread in several different nations and across different cultures, so there are many different ways that the faith is practiced in the day to day by its adherents. However, the Arysian Church has the following laws and precepts for its followers to obey:

  • Attend Mass on Sundays and days of obligation. Though some churches (particularly those in larger cities) may have mass every day, the Arysian Church does require that its followers attend mass every Sunday and on its days of obligation: The Day of Revelation (the first Sunday of Flamedawn), which celebrates Onyame’s first appearance to St. Arys; The Day of Ascension (the fifth day of Stormdusk), which celebrates St. Arys’ ascension into Heaven; Arsmas (the 14th of Highfell), which celebrates the birth of St. Arys; All Saints’ Day (the 1st of Harvestdawn), which commemorates the lives and deaths of all the saints; and The Assumption of St. Symon (the 9th of Highflame), which commemorates the end of St. Symon’s life and his body and soul being assumed into Heaven.
  • Fasting and abstinence on days of observance. Certain holidays and feast days are preceded by a period of fasting, typically practiced by giving up something (such as red meat or other luxurious foods) in order to prepare the soul for the holiday to come, and to help Arysians practice elevating their spiritual needs over their material desires.
  • Confession. Arysians must confess their sins at least once a year, in order to receive Onyame’s gift of forgiveness and be reconciled with Heaven. Only Onyame can forgive sins, and it is through the priests and confessors that Onyame grants people forgiveness. The priests themselves do not perform the act of forgiveness.
  • Tithing to provide for the needs of the Church. All Arysians must give according to their ability, in order to provide for the material needs of the Church, through which Onyame’s will is done.

Hierarchy. The Arysian Church is organized in a very strict hierarchical structure, consisting of archbishops, bishops, priests, with the pontifex above all. Every member of the clergy is required to swear vows of celibacy and are forbidden to marry, instead dedicating their lives to the Church and to Onyame.

  • Pontifex: The pontifex is the head of the Church, with the following titles: Bishop of Dorhem, Vicar of St. Arys, Successor of the First of the Apostles, Supreme Pontiff of the Universal Church, Patriarch of the North, Servant of the servants of Onyame. They have extreme authority over matters of theology and inner-Church politics, and prior to the establishment of the Empire, the pontifex was often called upon as the mediator for disputes between monarchs. The pontifex also has the power to excommunicate people from the Church, and pass judgment on crimes within and/or against the Church. Because the Arysian faith is also the state faith of the Empire, this gives the pontifex quite a bit of power over members of the Empire, as crimes against the Empire can thus be interpreted as crimes against the faith, allowing the pontifex to have a say in the judgement/punishment. The pontifex is appointed by the council of Archbishops, and remains in their position until death. The pontifex in turn appoints new archbishops. When a pontifex is named, they take the name of a saint.
  • Archbishops: Archbishops are chosen by the pontifex and oversee the appointment of each new pontifex, as well as the appointment of bishops in their respective jurisdictions. Their major duties are advising the pontifex and overseeing/running the Church in each nation. There are eight archbishops, two for each nation. One archbishop for each nation is selected to reside permanently in the Imperial Capital of Dorhem (the archbishop va Onyame), while one is selected to remain in the nation’s capital (the archbishop va itthon). Archbishops often serve as the spiritual advisors to their nation’s monarch.
  • Bishops: Bishops, similar to archbishops, are the heads of specific jurisdictions of the Church. Most bishops are stationed within large cities and oversee their city’s church as well as the churches in the surrounding area.
  • Priests: Priests sometimes travel around the Edhela spreading the good word, but more often they are the individual leaders of the churches in Edhela. Priests lead worship, offer blessings for children and preside over funerals, and serve as the spiritual leaders of whatever village they reside in. In order to be ordained, priests must first attend seminary and be educated in High Dwarrin, theology, and canon law.
  • Abbotts: Abbotts live in and oversee the Church’s monasteries, which are scattered throughout Edhela. They are often either appointed by their local bishop, or elected from within their monastery itself and confirmed by the bishop.
  • Monks: Within the Church, there are several monastic orders, dedicated to specific kinds of religious living, often associated with vows of poverty, obedience, and chastity, and living separate from society so that they may devote themselves to spirituality and obedience to Onyame above everything else.
  • Holy Knights: The Order of Holy Knights serves to protect and fight for the Church of Arys and carry out its commands. These armored warriors are commonly gifted with Light Magick in addition to their martial skills, and they are commonly called to defend the Church when its landed holdings are threatened or to seek out and destroy bands of heretics.

Magic. While wielding divine magic isn't rare, it is fairly uncommon in Edhela. Clerics are people who have been divinely blessed by God to carry out Their will in the world, and most of them are affiliated with the Church. The word 'cleric' denotes the magical capabilities of a person and is not a title, so while being a cleric will help you rise in the ranks of the church hierarchy, it isn't a special role in itself. The Church believes that divine magic is bestowed to only the most holy and devout people (which is why being a cleric will shoot you up through the church's ranks really fast) and indeed, most clerics are people who have lived and breathed the Church's teachings their entire lives. Clerics can lose their magic if they lose their faith, which the Church has incorporated into its doctrine as God exacting punishment on those who turn from Them by stripping them of their power. Every single pontifex of the Arysian Church has been a cleric.

There is magic that the Church views as heresy: necromancy, enchantment, and dark magic. Necromancy is the ultimate sin, as it abuses the body and corrupts the soul. Resurrection is considered impossible, so any who have been returned to life are considered to lack a soul and all involved are eternally damned—having permanently rended their soul from Onyame. Enchantment, as it takes away the Onyame given free will and agency, is similarly heretical due to how dangerous and destructive it can be.

Dark magic (also called witchcraft, pact magic, and the occult arts) is considered extremely heretical, as it channels power from the chaotic forces of Darkness in order to sow destruction upon the earth. Using dark magic corrupts and condemns the soul, and while such sins can be forgiven, it is the nature of dark magic to turn its user against the Light of Onyame and draw them further into Esum’s embrace, making repentance nigh impossible. The magic practiced by the druidic clans and followers of the Old Ways is considered by the Church to be dark magic.

Saints. Arysian saints are heroic historical figures of the Church. Saints lived incredibly holy lives and often did miraculous deeds or died for their faith, causing them to be honored long after their deaths. The saints mostly serve as examples that the faithful should strive towards, and some are even regarded as patrons of certain occupations or causes. Saints themselves are not worshiped, rather people ask saints to pray for them for specific things. A few popular examples:

  • St. Symon: The father and disciple of St. Arys. He is highly venerated by the Church, practically the second most important saint after St. Arys herself.
  • St. Isolde: The first elected pontifex, St. Isolde was the one who converted King Auden Glaziere to the Arysian faith and founded the Church.
  • St. Elisabeth: After losing her own spouse, Elisabeth turned to the Arysian faith and founded a monastery in her spouse's name. She’s often prayed to in times of grief and loss, particularly of spouses or children.

Marriage. The Arysian faith denies plural marriage, and marriage between Arysians and non-Arysians is prohibited. Divorce, however, is also accepted and practiced within the Arysian faith, for St. Arys taught that those unable to do justly with each other, or if one spouse suffered at the hands of another, should have their marriages ended, rather than continue to do harm.

Iconography. The main symbol of the Arysian Church is a yellow sun with eight rays flaring out from it, a symbolic representation of Onyame’s centrality in the universe (as the sun is the center of the universe in Edhelan cosmology), and Their nature as the giver of Light and Life to all things. Another symbol commonly associated with the Arysian church is that of a shepherd’s crook, as St. Arys was a shepherd before she was called by Onyame, and the symbolism of a shepherd with their flock is used frequently in Arysian parables describing the relationship between the Church and its people.

The Southern Church

The Southern Church is a branch of the Arysian faith created when the Edhelan Church and the Southern Church split apart during the Great Schism in 901 P.I.

Following a ruling by the pontifex that druidic magic was heretical, the archbishop va itthon of Meravía ruled in disagreement. Upon his excommunication, a large number of the Meravían archbishops declared the pontifex illegitimate, elevating the archbishop to the title instead. Since then, the Southern Church has operated independent of the Orthodox Church, with its own slightly altered Holy Chronicle and hierarchy.

The primary differences between the Southern Church and the Orthodox Church in Edhela are that the Southern Church allows priest marriage, that the Southern Church does not deem natural/druidic magic to be heresy, and that the Southern Church believes in the existence and intercession of angels, which the Orthodox Church condemns as heresy.

The Old Ways

The “Old Ways” are the religious practices of the north that existed before the Church of Arys, and now are practiced almost exclusively by the druidic clans of the mountains and some in the Meian Isles.

The Old Ways are very animistic, with followers believing that all things in nature are imbued with life and spirit, and these spirits can be worshipped and deified, though the specific practices often vary from place to place. In the Meian Isles, the goddess of the Sea, Meia, is worshipped by many, and followers venerate her by offering a part of every feast to the goddess. The Old Ways may also be practiced by maintaining shrines to the nature spirits, worshipping in circular temples in groves of trees, and offering votive sacrifices to the gods by burying offerings in the ground near the roots of trees.

  • Meia. The spirit of the Northern Sea, Meia is the goddess most revered by the people of the Meian Isles. One of the ancient legends says there were people living in the North in Giant Country. They were small and weak, and so the Giants terrorized them, destroying their villages and eating their livestock. The people cried out on the shores of the sea, and their tears mixed with the waves. Meia took pity on the people and from their tears she created islands. Then she took wood from the ruins of their villages to create a boat which carried the people to safety, away from the giants.

With the advent of the Church of Arys, much of the Old Faiths have been lost to time, though remnants of their traditions and practices remain weaved into Arysian practice. For example, Koliada, a winter festival that honored the harvest and mourned the loss of the Sun, is still practiced but with a distinctly Arysian flavor: giving thanks to God for a good harvest, and praying for Them to see the people through the winter. In the mountains and forests of Paerdland, it is common to come across prayer stones, large stones carved with prayers and the symbol of the Arysian church. It’s customary for travelers to stop at these stones to pray and carve their own prayers/blessings into the rock.

Magic. Magic is often practiced by those who follow the Old Ways, and one of the held tenets of the Old Ways is that the gods/spirits exist in the world alongside people, and through interacting with them, people can be blessed with magical power. Many ancient legends tell stories of warriors who were visited by the gods and took on quests to receive their blessings, people who a god fell in love with and took as their spouse, children of nature spirits and mortals, etc.

Oriande. Like Paerdland, Oriande is completely Arysian with the exception of the druidic clans roaming the mountains to its eastern border. However, before the Arysian Church in the days of the Orvhallen Empire, Oriande had its own pantheon of gods that were far different from the nature spirits deified by its Paerdish neighbors. In the centuries since the rise of the Arysian Church followed by the conversion and subsequent fall of the Orvhallen Empire, the names of that pantheon of gods have been quite literally lost. There is no one alive who knows the names of these old gods, and any recording of any of the gods’ names on a temple wall or written in ancient papyrus appears destroyed or burned away. The Arysian Church claims that this is simply Onyame’s primacy made manifest, that Oriande’s false idols were struck down by the might of Their Will. More superstitious and heretical folk tell stories about the gods being killed or fading from existence as their followers turned away from their worship and taking their names with them.

Annals of Edhela and the Known World

2500 - 2000 Priori Imperium

  • 2375 - The Orvhallen Empire rises in the western plains of Edhela (modern Oriande). The empire is ruled by an imperial family, House Epoloneos, who rule from their imperial capital in Vatera and slowly begin to conquer and subjugate all of Oriande.
  • 2156 - The northern fiefs of Edhela are united by Ingmar Glaziere to found the Kingdom of Paerdland.

1999 - 1500 Priori Imperium

  • 1952 - After the discovery of magic, Thalore is founded by House Liamenor, a noble family of wizards who use their newfound arcane power to conquer their neighbors and unite the southern estates into a single kingdom.
  • 1631 - The Orvhallen Empire begins expanding past the mountains and conquering territory in Paerdland.
  • 1609 - The Royal House Glaziere is forced to flee to the island of Fnjoska as the Orvhallen Empire overruns the Paerdish forces defending the royal capital of Keldholme. Much of Paerdish territory falls into Orvhallen control, and Orvhallen military outposts are established across the north, bringing Orvhallen culture, religion, and societal norms with them (such as patriarchal society) as well as the suppression of many traditional northern customs, often by violent means.
  • 1607 - Arys (later canonized as St. Arys) hears the voice of Onyame in the mountains (year 1 according to the Arysian calendar) and begins preaching her good news to the people of Paerdland.
  • 1603 - St. Arys disappears, and her followers spread the word that she has been taken up into the heavens by Onyame to join Them. The remaining followers of Arys continue their worship and evangelism in small cult-like cells around Paerdland, often being martyred and violently oppressed by the Orvhallen occupation.
  • 1572 - House Liamenor is overthrown after years of despotism and civil war, and House Davila seizes control of the Thaloran throne. Remaining members of House Liamenor take up residence in the independent kingdom of Emirselia, off of Thalore’s southern coast.

1499 - 1000 Priori Imperium

  • 1489 - Exiled Paerdish Queen Saoirse Glaziere gathers enough support from the jarls of the Meian Isles to begin trying to retake Paerdland from the Orvhallen Imperial occupation, marking the beginning of the Reclamation wars.
  • 1435 - Queen Saoirse dies in battle and her son, Auden, is crowned king of Paerdland. Auden’s right hand, an Arysian cleric named Isolde, dreams of a Paerdish victory against the Orvhallen occupation, but only if Auden takes up the banner of St. Arys and converts to the faith. Auden does, and Isolde (later canonized as St. Isolde) blesses the shield that he carries into war (now considered a powerful holy relic).
  • 1421 - The Reclamation Wars come to an end when the combined Paerdish/Meian forces retake Keldholme and drive the Orvhallen occupation back over the mountains. St. Isolde is rewarded for his part in Paerdland’s victory when King Auden proclaims the Arysian faith to be the faith of Paerdland and grants Isolde the city of Dorhem (creating the first bishopric), for him and his followers to establish their new Church.
  • 1419 - The First Council of Dorhem is held in Dorhem, during which the first properly recorded papal election is held to elect Isolde as the first pontifex of Dorhem. For the first time, the disorganized and cult-like followers of Arys begin to determine and solidify the rules and doctrine that will universally govern the body of Arys’ Church.
  • 1418 - The first Holy Chronicle of St. Arys is compiled at the Second Council of Dorhem.
  • 1098 P.I. - The Arysian Church splits during the Great Schism when Meravía breaks off from the mainland Church over theological differences about the nature of magic. The Southern Church appoints its first pontifex, Eliseo Leoz.

999 - 500 Priori Imperium

  • 863 - Queen Maura ter Davila of Thalore dies without an heir, and a brief but brutal succession war breaks out between claimants Ruven ter Davila, Caelia ter Aendryndel, and Piero ter Laemirsel. Caelia ter Aendryndel, the former queen’s niece by an illegitimate sister and the only female claimant, wins the war and is crowned Queen of Thalore.
  • 726 - King Eamon of Paerdland draws the anger of the pontifex after appointing three new bishops in Paerdland, counter to the Church’s doctrine banning lay investiture. As a result, King Eamon declares that the crown of Paerdland has the only supreme power in Edhela, having granted the Church lands and rights in the first place, and calls for the election of a new pontifex. Pontifex Eumenius excommunicates the king.
  • 724 - After several rebellions from his vassals in response to his excommunication, King Eamon begs the forgiveness of the pontifex and after doing penance, is pardoned. Pontifex Eumenius continues to lend his support to rebellious Paerdish nobles.
  • 722 - Pontifex Eumenius dies and is replaced by Pontifex Eugenia II, who is far more favorable to King Eamon. Under Eugenia’s leadership, a compromise is reached, maintaining the Church’s sole authority over the investiture of the clergy but allowing secular rulers to retain taxes paid from lands controlled by bishops within their desmesnes.
  • 688 - Jarl Toranna Hafschilde of Kvanne and her heirs are all killed in a Hraezlan raid on the isle. A council is convened of the nobles and warriors of Kvanne to choose a new jarl. After nearly a week of discussion and performing feats of strength, Orin Hjorschilde is elected as the new jarl of Kvanne.
  • 574 - Quintus Rabireos, a relative of and high ranking member of Emperor Fabio Epoloneos’ court, makes a move for the Orvhallen throne and succeeds, deposing his cousin. The Epoloneos family is exiled from Vatera, and flees to northern Oriande.
  • 573 - Civil war breaks out in Oriande when the Epoloneos family gathers an army and marches on Vatera to reclaim their empire.
  • 549 - The civil war ends and Paesentia Epoloneos becomes emperor, making her the first and only female ruler of the Orvhallen Empire. Paesentia has Quintus Rabireos and his supporters executed.
  • 543 - Paesentia’s mother, who had already converted to the Arysian faith, suades Paesentia into converting to the Arysian faith and declaring the Edict of Pisae, declaring tolerance for the Arysian faith in the Orvhallen Empire, which up to that point had often been ruthless and violent in its suppression of Arysian beliefs, leading to the veneration of many Oriandi martyr saints.

499 Priori Imperium - 0 Era Imperium

  • 463 - Queen Aelerynne ter Aendryndel of Thalore musters forces to begin an invasion of the kingdom of Emirselia in order to conquer it, marking the first of the Thalor-Emirselian wars, which would last the next century or so.
  • 414 - After years of expansion by the Kingdom of Thalore into the Orvhallen Empire’s eastern territories, Emperor Manius Epoloneos invades Thalore in what would be known as the Irym War. Brutally unprepared for battle with Thalore’s wizard army, the Orvhallen invasion of Thalore fails and the war soon moves to Oriande as Thalore strikes back at the heart of the empire.
  • Thalore is forced to withdraw its occupying forces from Emirselia in order to defend against the Orvhallen invasion. Emirselian rebels quickly seize control of the country and install Essaer ter Laemirsel as the new king of independent Emirselia.
  • 412 - After decades of decline, the Orvhallen Empire falls with the end of the Irym War, when the Thaloran army’s siege of Vatera is successful. Vatera is sacked, and Emperor Manius Epoloneos and his family are killed.
  • 398 - After a 14 year occupation, Thalore agrees to leave Oriande, though much of the Orvhallen Empire’s territory is acquired by Thalore in the process. A distant Epoloneos cousin, Draco Voltareos, is installed by Thalore as the new emperor.
  • 396 - Emperor Draco Voltareos is assassinated in Vatera, and Oriande is once again thrown into chaos.
  • A branch of Draco Voltareos’ family, the Trandeos, try to seek the throne, none have a claim to Epoloneos ancestry and are rejected by Vatera.
  • 395 - King Thelan of Paerdland faces a revolt from his barons, led by his younger twin brother, Prince Ailbert, as a result of unpopular taxes spent raising forces to invade Giant territory in the far north. Prince Ailbert manages to capture the king and his husband, and assumes rule of the country, allegedly in the king’s name.
  • Seven months later, Thelan is smuggled out of Keldholme to Dorhem, where he appeals to Pontifex Johanna IX to step in and arbitrate the dispute. Pontifex Johanna declares against the rebels and condemns Prince Ailbert. King Thelan musters forces from Paerdish loyalists and Holy Knights to resume conflict against his twin brother.
  • 394 - General Kaeso Marteos orders his remaining Imperial troops to get the capital under control, and declares a new government: the Oriande Commonwealth.
  • The Trandeos family declares themselves the Imperial Family in exile, declaring the city of Izmir their capital. They retain contested control over most of northern and central Oriande with the Commonwealth in Vatera.
  • In the chaos, numerous cities throughout Oriande seize their independence, establishing a variety of republican and warlord regional powers. The southern city of Develtos forms a Council of Luminaries modeled after Meravía, intent to establish itself as a naval power.
  • 393 - King Thelan recaptures Keldholme and imprisons his twin brother.
  • Ailbert dies in prison less than a year later, and rumor spreads that he was poisoned by the king.
  • 391 - With the end of the Irym War, Thalore refocuses on the conquest of Emirselia, managing to recapture much of the island’s territory, sending the deposed king Aemyn ter Laemirsel fleeing to the Republic of Develtos in southern Oriande.
  • Queen Elaenna ter Aendryndel levies incredibly high taxes on her lords to begin constructing new forts and castles across Emirselia to deepen Thalore’s hold on the land.
  • 389 - The first Moon War between the Commonwealth and Trandeos Izmir breaks out as the Trandeos family tries to retake Vatera, using primarily mercenaries made up of Paerdish and former imperial soldiers.
  • 386 - A former Orvhallen general Regulus Trandeos, who fought for the Trandeos in the First Moon War, takes his remnant force and turns it on the city of Arketsa, declaring himself its lord.
  • 375 - Aemyn ter Laemirsel returns to Emirselia with a new force made up of Oriandi mercenaries and exiled Emirselian lords to break Thalore’s hold on the country and liberate Emirselia completely.
  • 372 - Queen Lyneth ter Aendryndel attempts to muster forces to retake Emirselia, but the high levies raised in order to finance the endeavor make her nobles balk at the prospect and threaten civil war. Lyneth’s attempt is stopped in its tracks.
  • 369 - King Aemyn of Emirselia dies without an obvious heir, and Queen Lyneth quickly chooses a claimant to back as a puppet ruler, lending Owaen ter Laemirsel funds and armies needed to win the brief conflict, and he bows to Thalore as a vassal of its kingdom.
  • 368 - An unsuccessful rebellion against Owaen ter Laemirsel is swiftly put down by Thaloran forces.
  • 363 - Owaen ter Laemirsel is assassinated by Emirselian rebels. Emirselia devolves into chaos and conflict, with Thalore and the Republic of Develtos both vying for influence over the island. The anarchy ends when Emirselia is partitioned between Thaloran-controlled territory and an independent Emirselian kingdom, supported by Develtos.
  • 349 - The second Moon War between the Commonwealth and Trandeos Izmir initially over control of farmland on the Irym river, concluding in another failed attempt by the Trandeos to seize total control of northern Oriande.
  • 342 - Thalore finally wins total control of Emirselia after the wedding of Crown Princess Taeryn ter Aendryndel to Raen ter Laemirsel II, the lord of independent Emirselia, uniting the kingdoms. Their daughter inherits the crowns of both Emirselia and Thalore, though she bestows rule of the duchy of Emirselia to her younger brother, Owaen.
  • 291 - Duchess Anselda Merein of Idsal dies without issue. Idsal instead passes to her nearest cousin, Frida Skardeschilde, a Meian warrior who declares herself jarl of Idsal.
  • 290 - Jarl Frida of Idsal faces a popular revolt in Idsal from her barons and common folk, people who consider themselves Paerdish and now unhappy at being ruled by a “jarl” from the North. This revolt is put down with the help of Frida’s Meian allies, and King Aodmer of Paerdland acknowledges that Idsal is part of the Meian Isles.
  • 268 - Consul Gaius Palleos is assassinated in Izmir by Trandeos agents during a diplomatic visit, igniting The third Moon War. The war concludes with the execution of the Trandeos family and the harsh subjugation of Izmir under the Commonwealth.
  • 203 - When his father is unexpectedly killed in a hunting accident, three year old Ernesto Trandeos is deposed by his cousin Adriana Hypaerion, leaving the city under Paerdish control.
  • 149 - The Oriande Commonwealth ousts the Hypaerion family from Arketsa, declaring the city a part of the Commonwealth.
  • 132 - Queen Alyndis I of Thalore marries Duke Charles II of Ilacante, bringing the formerly independent duchy under Thaloran rule.
  • 101 - Louis ter Aendryndel, eldest son of Queen Alyndis and Duke Charles, secures a marriage alliance with Paerdland, which he leverages to support his own armed forces in forcibly claiming the duchy of Ilacante for himself after Thaloran succession law endowed his younger sister with the duchy instead of him.
  • 100 - Louis ter Aendryndel and his mother come to terms and the lands of Ilacante are divided, giving some to Louis and the rest to his younger sister, Rhydian.
  • 79 - Border disputes between the Commonwealth of Oriande and the Republic of Develtos breaks out into the beginning of what would be known as the Reformation Wars. Using the conflict’s momentum, Consul Marianus Voluseos leads the Commonwealth through a series of conquests of the scattered independent city-states holding out against its control.
  • Over the course of his highly successful campaign, Consul Voluseos is granted increasingly expanded war powers, ultimately being declared Dictator for Life.
  • 61 - The final holdout city against the Commonwealth, Lanuvum, is defeated in its cause to remain independent, ending the Reformation Wars and uniting Oriande for the first time since the Irym Wars. Consul Voluseos is slain by a stray arrow during the final assault.
  • 40 - After a series of border disputes between Thalore and Paerdland regarding control of Ilacante, the Great War begins with Thalore’s invasion of Ilacante and later, Paerdland.
  • Thaloran nobles hire several Oriandi mercenary companies alongside their own armies of mages. Their initial strike is swift and devastating, wreaking chaos and destruction along Paerdland’s southern borders and further north towards Paerdland’s capital of Keldholme.
  • 37 - Oriande declares its alliance with Thalore, joining the war in a more official capacity, sending the Republican army eastward to attack Paerdland.
  • 35 - After a devastating four year siege, with the help of their Meian allies, Paerdland is able to break the siege of Keldholme and begins counterattacking, beckoning in decades of back-and-forth warfare.
  • 15 - Powerful Thaloran mages (likely members of high ranking noble families, though the exact identities remain unknown) making use of new teleportation spells begin a devastating series of magical strikes against villages and cities in the far north of Paerdland. This begins to tip the war back into Thalore’s favor as Paerdish cities and villages are destroyed and ransacked, stripping the Paerdish forces of crucial supplies for their war effort.
  • 9 - Wealthy families in northern Oriande begin sending aid in secret to Paerdish forces via the northern sea, bolstering the Paerdish/Meian armies.
  • 10 - Queen Cerelia dies of old age, and Ceolmunde Glaziere takes the throne of Paerdland.
  • 5 - With the election of Consul Tullia Galleos, Oriande formally breaks its alliance with Thalore, joining up with Paerdland and the Meian Isles.
  • In what is known as “Galleos’ Slaughter”, several Oriande mercenary companies in the employ of Thalore turn on their employers thanks to secret negotiations by Consul Galleos to outbid their contracts.
  • Thaloran forces are pushed back into their own territory, and the war is now fought on Thaloran soil.

1 - 40 Era Imperium

  • 1 Era Imperium - The Great War ends after the combined northern and Oriandi armies reach Badura, the capital of Thalore, and the young and newly crowned Queen Adthana ter Aendryndel surrenders.
  • Several weeks of negotiations in the Paerdish city of Dorhem result in the signing of the Edict of Edhela, a new peace treaty that would found a new empire to unite and rule over all of the four nations. Rosalinde Hypaerion is elected and crowned as the sovereign of this new Holy Edhelan Empire, ruling over the nations of Paerdland, Thalore, Oriande, and the Meian Isles.
  • 10 - Tensions rise between the Queen Adthana of Thalore and her high ranking lords, created by the high financial burden borne by Thalore in the wake of the Edict of Edhela and the taxes levied against the nation by the imperial crown for the rebuilding of Paerdland. Adthana’s perceived weakness by her lords in her continual submission to the empire, as well as her overreliance on her council of advisors (particularly her father, the Dowager King Dario ter Ravalynn), leads some of them to begin to refuse their imperial taxes.
  • 11 - Alaen ter Ravalynn, chancellor of the Thaloran Royal Exchequer and cousin of the queen, and his escort of Aendryndel soldiers are murdered on the road on their way to perform an audit of House Galakir’s finances. Spurred by her council and the anger of her father’s family, Queen Adthana musters forces to march against House Galakir, sparking the Marquises’ Rebellion.
  • 13 - Queen Adthana petitions the empire for aid in putting down her rebellious nobles but Oriande, Paerdland, and the Meian Isles refuse, preventing the imperial army from marching. Rumors allege that one of the Oriandi consuls refused Adthana’s request so that his family’s mercenary company could extend its contract with its Thaloran employer.
  • 18 - Adthana wins the allegiance of House Nevarro and brings them to the loyalist side by marrying the Duchess’ daughter, Mariona ter Nevarro.
  • 20 - Spurred to violence by its firebrand bishop, the city of Izmir rises in rebellion against Vatera, demanding it be recognized as a separate republic under the empire. The senate calls upon Emperor Rosalinde to use the imperial armies and press the city back into submission, leading to one of the most brutal massacres in recent Edhelan history.
  • 23 - After over a decade of civil war, Adthana, with the help of the newly elected Pontifex Margery, negotiates a peace with her rebellious lords. As a part of the terms of peace, Adthana agrees to a new measure that would require majority approval from her high council of dukes in order to cast a vote for the use of the imperial armies.
  • 40 - Today.
